item.title: @wallstengine: NIKE RETURNS TO FORMULA 1 AFTER 24 YEARS $NKE has signed a long-term partnership with Formula 1, re...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NIKE RETURNS TO FORMULA 1 AFTER 24 YEARS
$NKE has signed a long-term partnership with Formula 1, replacing Puma as the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier starting in the 2027 season.
The deal will see Nike produce uniforms for F1 staff, along with F1-branded shoes, clothing and accessories for fans. Nike will also supply apparel for F1 Academy, the racing series focused on developing female drivers.
The partnership kicks off today, November 20, with a limited-edition Nike x Las Vegas Grand Prix collection available at select locations in Las Vegas.
Nike's last major involvement in Formula 1 was through its footwear partnership with seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher, which ended in 2002.
item.content:encoded:
NIKE RETURNS TO FORMULA 1 AFTER 24 YEARS

$NKE has signed a long-term partnership with Formula 1, replacing Puma as the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier starting in the 2027 season.

The deal will see Nike produce uniforms for F1 staff, along with F1-branded shoes, clothing and accessories for fans. Nike will also supply apparel for F1 Academy, the racing series focused on developing female drivers.

The partnership kicks off today, November 20, with a limited-edition Nike x Las Vegas Grand Prix collection available at select locations in Las Vegas.

Nike's last major involvement in Formula 1 was through its footwear partnership with seven-time world champion Michael Schumacher, which ended in 2002.

item.title: @wallstengine: Citigroup $C underestimated its risk-weighted assets by about $35B after incorrectly recording trad...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Citigroup $C underestimated its risk-weighted assets by about $35B after incorrectly recording trades at its UK securities unit.
The bank used an internal risk model that regulators hadn't approved for those transactions. When the trades were recalculated using the correct model, the amount of assets used to determine Citi's required capital reserves jumped by roughly $35B.
Citi says it identified and fixed the issue this summer and injected additional capital into its European subsidiary to restore its financial buffers.
The bank says the subsidiary remained above regulatory minimum capital requirements throughout.
item.content:encoded:
Citigroup $C underestimated its risk-weighted assets by about $35B after incorrectly recording trades at its UK securities unit.

The bank used an internal risk model that regulators hadn't approved for those transactions. When the trades were recalculated using the correct model, the amount of assets used to determine Citi's required capital reserves jumped by roughly $35B.

Citi says it identified and fixed the issue this summer and injected additional capital into its European subsidiary to restore its financial buffers.

The bank says the subsidiary remained above regulatory minimum capital requirements throughout.

item.title: @wallstengine: HSBC upgrades $TSLA from Reduce to Hold and raises its price target to $359 from $157, citing a pot...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
HSBC upgrades $TSLA from Reduce to Hold and raises its price target to $359 from $157, citing a potential acquisition by SpaceX.
The bank now values Tesla using two scenarios:
SpaceX acquisition: $507/share.
Standalone valuation: $212/share, up from $193, based on Tesla's underlying businesses.
HSBC assigns a 50% weighting to each scenario, resulting in its new $359 target.
"Given the acquisition newsflow, we believe the current share price of Tesla offers an anchor, irrespective of the fundamentals."
However, HSBC acknowledges there is no guarantee a deal will happen or receive shareholder approval, and that Tesla could trade on its fundamentals alone if an acquisition does not materialize.
item.content:encoded:
HSBC upgrades $TSLA from Reduce to Hold and raises its price target to $359 from $157, citing a potential acquisition by SpaceX.

The bank now values Tesla using two scenarios:

SpaceX acquisition: $507/share.

Standalone valuation: $212/share, up from $193, based on Tesla's underlying businesses.

HSBC assigns a 50% weighting to each scenario, resulting in its new $359 target.

"Given the acquisition newsflow, we believe the current share price of Tesla offers an anchor, irrespective of the fundamentals."

However, HSBC acknowledges there is no guarantee a deal will happen or receive shareholder approval, and that Tesla could trade on its fundamentals alone if an acquisition does not materialize.

item.title: @wallstengine: CHINA 🇨🇳 SEEKS TO RESTART U.S. PRIVATE EQUITY INVESTMENTS: FT China's sovereign wealth fund, Chin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CHINA 🇨🇳 SEEKS TO RESTART U.S. PRIVATE EQUITY INVESTMENTS: FT
China's sovereign wealth fund, China Investment Corporation, is negotiating terms with private equity firms that would allow Chinese investors to recover their money if U.S. or European sanctions are imposed, without forcing funds to sell their assets.
Proposals include repayment arrangements tied to fund exits, separate investment vehicles and provisions allowing investors to opt out of individual deals.
Chinese state-backed investors stopped making new U.S. private equity commitments during last year's trade war, after previously backing firms including Blackstone, Carlyle, Thoma Bravo and Vista Equity.
Fund advisers say Trump's recent China visit helped revive CIC's interest, although no new investment commitments have been announced.
item.content:encoded:
CHINA 🇨🇳 SEEKS TO RESTART U.S. PRIVATE EQUITY INVESTMENTS: FT

China's sovereign wealth fund, China Investment Corporation, is negotiating terms with private equity firms that would allow Chinese investors to recover their money if U.S. or European sanctions are imposed, without forcing funds to sell their assets.

Proposals include repayment arrangements tied to fund exits, separate investment vehicles and provisions allowing investors to opt out of individual deals.

Chinese state-backed investors stopped making new U.S. private equity commitments during last year's trade war, after previously backing firms including Blackstone, Carlyle, Thoma Bravo and Vista Equity.

Fund advisers say Trump's recent China visit helped revive CIC's interest, although no new investment commitments have been announced.

item.title: @wallstengine: Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for more than $500M, plus potential emp...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nvidia is in advanced talks to acquire AI startup Inception for more than $500M, plus potential employee earnouts, The Information reports.
Inception develops diffusion-based language models designed to generate responses faster than traditional AI models like those powering ChatGPT and Claude.
Nvidia plans to use Inception's technology and researchers to strengthen its Nemotron open-weight models and AI systems for robotics.
All three co-founders are expected to join Nvidia. Microsoft had also expressed interest in a similar deal before Nvidia's talks advanced.

item.title: @wallstengine: WHITE HOUSE NATIONAL CYBER DIRECTOR SEAN CAIRNCROSS RESIGNS - AXIOS Cairncross leads the Office of...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
WHITE HOUSE NATIONAL CYBER DIRECTOR SEAN CAIRNCROSS RESIGNS - AXIOS
Cairncross leads the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy and strategy across the federal government. The job requires Senate confirmation.
He did not want to serve another two years, and is leaving now to give the White House time to secure Senate confirmation of a successor before Democrats take control of the Senate in January, according to two sources. Axios describes the departure as amicable.
His head of policy and senior adviser, Thomas Lind, left in June and joined OpenAI in October.
On Monday, Cairncross told Semafor that a cyberattack was not behind the nationwide air traffic ground stop and other outages, blaming upgrades to old technology.
The White House has not yet responded to Axios' request for comment.

His head of policy and senior adviser, Thomas Lind, left in June and joined OpenAI in October.

On Monday, Cairncross told Semafor that a cyberattack was not behind the nationwide air traffic ground stop and other outages, blaming upgrades to old technology.

item.title: @wallstengine: $AAPL IS DEVELOPING ITS OWN AI AGENT TO CONTROL DEVICES, BROWSE THE WEB & WRITE CODE New job listin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AAPL IS DEVELOPING ITS OWN AI AGENT TO CONTROL DEVICES, BROWSE THE WEB & WRITE CODE
New job listings reveal Apple is building an autonomous AI assistant that can carry out tasks on users' behalf, including:
- Control apps and navigate devices - Browse the web, run commands and write or debug code - Plan and execute multistep tasks across apps and services - Coordinate multiple specialized AI agents
Apple has considered launching the service as early as late 2027, though development is still in its early stages.
Meanwhile, Apple is tightening permissions for competing AI agents on Macs. In macOS 27.3, enabling ChatGPT's computer-use capabilities now requires 14 steps, up from four previously, according to Bloomberg.
item.content:encoded:
$AAPL IS DEVELOPING ITS OWN AI AGENT TO CONTROL DEVICES, BROWSE THE WEB & WRITE CODE

New job listings reveal Apple is building an autonomous AI assistant that can carry out tasks on users' behalf, including:

- Control apps and navigate devices
- Browse the web, run commands and write or debug code
- Plan and execute multistep tasks across apps and services
- Coordinate multiple specialized AI agents

Apple has considered launching the service as early as late 2027, though development is still in its early stages.

Meanwhile, Apple is tightening permissions for competing AI agents on Macs. In macOS 27.3, enabling ChatGPT's computer-use capabilities now requires 14 steps, up from four previously, according to Bloomberg.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA & MICROSOFT EXPAND AI PARTNERSHIP FROM AZURE DATA CENTERS TO WINDOWS PCS Nvidia and Microsoft...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA & MICROSOFT EXPAND AI PARTNERSHIP FROM AZURE DATA CENTERS TO WINDOWS PCS
Nvidia and Microsoft $MSFT announced several new AI infrastructure and software integrations at Microsoft Ignite, covering cloud computing, enterprise AI models, robotics and local AI.
Here are the key developments:
Vera Rubin on Azure: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are already running in Microsoft's data centers, with Azure expanding access to Rubin-powered infrastructure for AI training, reasoning and inference.
Enterprise AI models: Microsoft Foundry is expanding support for Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 open models, allowing companies to customize AI models using their own data and deploy them through Microsoft's cloud services.
55% accuracy improvement, 15x lower cost: EY used Nvidia Nemotron through Microsoft Foundry to improve the accuracy of corporate purchasing-record classification by 55% while reducing costs by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models in its evaluation.
AI on local servers and PCs: Azure Local is adding support for Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and Jetson platforms for industrial AI and robotics. The companies are also demonstrating AI models running directly on Windows PCs powered by RTX Spark.
Microsoft's own AI development: Microsoft AI is using Nvidia Dynamo software to accelerate inference during model post-training, while Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs are being used for Bing search models.
The companies are also expanding confidential computing to protect sensitive enterprise models and data during processing on Vera Rubin infrastructure.
item.content:encoded:
$NVDA & MICROSOFT EXPAND AI PARTNERSHIP FROM AZURE DATA CENTERS TO WINDOWS PCS

Nvidia and Microsoft $MSFT announced several new AI infrastructure and software integrations at Microsoft Ignite, covering cloud computing, enterprise AI models, robotics and local AI.

Here are the key developments:

Vera Rubin on Azure: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are already running in Microsoft's data centers, with Azure expanding access to Rubin-powered infrastructure for AI training, reasoning and inference.

Enterprise AI models: Microsoft Foundry is expanding support for Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 open models, allowing companies to customize AI models using their own data and deploy them through Microsoft's cloud services.

55% accuracy improvement, 15x lower cost: EY used Nvidia Nemotron through Microsoft Foundry to improve the accuracy of corporate purchasing-record classification by 55% while reducing costs by 15x compared with proprietary frontier models in its evaluation.

AI on local servers and PCs: Azure Local is adding support for Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs and Jetson platforms for industrial AI and robotics. The companies are also demonstrating AI models running directly on Windows PCs powered by RTX Spark.

Microsoft's own AI development: Microsoft AI is using Nvidia Dynamo software to accelerate inference during model post-training, while Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs are being used for Bing search models.

The companies are also expanding confidential computing to protect sensitive enterprise models and data during processing on Vera Rubin infrastructure.

Meta plans to price its pocket-sized Muse Charm AI device at $300, with up to 12 months of free Verizon 5G service to access its Muse AI assistant.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NETFLIX, AMAZON, YOUTUBE & FOX EXPECTED TO BID FOR 2030 FIFA WORLD CUP U.S. MEDIA RIGHTS
First-round bids are due today, with media executives expecting the winning offer to reach around $1.5 billion or more, CNBC reports.
Disney/ESPN is out after deciding it couldn't justify the price, even with a partner. Apple and Skydance also won't bid, while NBCUniversal/Telemundo remains undecided.
FIFA prefers to sell English and Spanish rights together and plans to select a winner by year-end.
A streaming winner would not be required to make any games available on free TV.
Source: CNBC
item.content:encoded:

First-round bids are due today, with media executives expecting the winning offer to reach around $1.5 billion or more, CNBC reports.

Disney/ESPN is out after deciding it couldn't justify the price, even with a partner. Apple and Skydance also won't bid, while NBCUniversal/Telemundo remains undecided.

FIFA prefers to sell English and Spanish rights together and plans to select a winner by year-end.

A streaming winner would not be required to make any games available on free TV.

item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Volatility tells you which game you're playing.
$VIX below 19, investable.
Above 19, the Chop bucket. The bottom of the range starts falling out. Lower lows, big lower highs, and the selling picks up pace.
Volatility in the 30s, the F*ck bucket. Ranges widen and moves get violent.
Know your bucket before you size your position. #Process

item.title: @wallstengine: HUNTERBROOK REPORTS $AMD FIRMWARE APPEARED IN SOFTWARE UPDATES FROM A U.S.-BLACKLISTED CHINESE SERV...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
HUNTERBROOK REPORTS $AMD FIRMWARE APPEARED IN SOFTWARE UPDATES FROM A U.S.-BLACKLISTED CHINESE SERVER MAKER
Hunterbrook's new investigation into AMD found that IEIT Systems, a Chinese server manufacturer blacklisted by the U.S. in March 2025, continued posting server software updates containing newer AMD firmware after the restrictions took effect.
Key findings:
• Firmware updates: IEIT posted at least six server BIOS updates containing newer versions of AMD's firmware after being blacklisted, including an update posted October 19, 2026.
• Linked companies: Hunterbrook found that three other server vendors, Aivres, Kaytus and Maginfra, published firmware files that were 99.94% identical to IEIT's. Kaytus identifies IEIT as its ultimate parent.
• AI chips: AMD's own website lists Aivres as a partner offering servers powered by its Instinct AI accelerators, including the MI300X and MI325X.
• China revenue: AMD generated $7.75B, or 22.4% of its 2025 revenue, from customers billed in China and Hong Kong.
• Supply chain: Two Chinese joint ventures controlled by Tongfu Microelectronics perform most of AMD's chip assembly, testing and packaging. AMD purchased roughly $2B in services from them in 2025.
AMD did not answer Hunterbrook's questions about whether it held export licenses for the companies involved.
The investigation does not establish that AMD violated export laws or determine how IEIT obtained the firmware.
Hunterbrook Capital disclosed that it was short $AMD at the time of publication.
item.content:encoded:
HUNTERBROOK REPORTS $AMD FIRMWARE APPEARED IN SOFTWARE UPDATES FROM A U.S.-BLACKLISTED CHINESE SERVER MAKER

Hunterbrook's new investigation into AMD found that IEIT Systems, a Chinese server manufacturer blacklisted by the U.S. in March 2025, continued posting server software updates containing newer AMD firmware after the restrictions took effect.

Key findings:

• Firmware updates: IEIT posted at least six server BIOS updates containing newer versions of AMD's firmware after being blacklisted, including an update posted October 19, 2026.

• Linked companies: Hunterbrook found that three other server vendors, Aivres, Kaytus and Maginfra, published firmware files that were 99.94% identical to IEIT's. Kaytus identifies IEIT as its ultimate parent.

• AI chips: AMD's own website lists Aivres as a partner offering servers powered by its Instinct AI accelerators, including the MI300X and MI325X.

• China revenue: AMD generated $7.75B, or 22.4% of its 2025 revenue, from customers billed in China and Hong Kong.

• Supply chain: Two Chinese joint ventures controlled by Tongfu Microelectronics perform most of AMD's chip assembly, testing and packaging. AMD purchased roughly $2B in services from them in 2025.

AMD did not answer Hunterbrook's questions about whether it held export licenses for the companies involved.

The investigation does not establish that AMD violated export laws or determine how IEIT obtained the firmware.

Hunterbrook Capital disclosed that it was short $AMD at the time of publication.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Anthropic rings the opening bell at Nasdaq following its record $81.3B IPO, which drew demand for nearly 7x the shares offered.
Here's who got shares:
Retail: About 15% of the IPO.
Institutions: Most received no shares as existing backers were prioritized, per Bloomberg.
Japan: Investors received about $3B, at the low end of the planned $3B to $3.5B allocation.
UK Retail: Over 100,000 UK investors participated, with nearly two-thirds receiving their full allocation.
Private placements: A separate $26B investment from seven tech companies at the $83 IPO price:
Google: $10B Nvidia: $10B AMD: $2.5B Broadcom: $1B Micron: $1B Microsoft: $1B TSMC: $500M
The private placement is separate from the $81.3B public offering, with investors receiving non-voting shares.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -3.2 million barrels last week, to 276.4 milli...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -3.2 million barrels last week, to 276.4 million barrels, its lowest level since August 1982.
This follows declines of -2.65 million barrels and -399,000 barrels in the previous two weeks.
Since the March high, US SPR inventories have collapsed -139.1 million barrels, or -34%, down in 33 of the last 34 weeks.
The SPR now stands -450.3 million barrels, or -62%, below its all-time high set in 2010.
This is also just 5.9 million barrels above its lowest level on record, set in the week ending August 20th, 1982.
US oil reserves have rarely been this low.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The S&P 500 has recorded 25 trading days with daily losses of at least -1% so far in 2026. This inc...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The S&P 500 has recorded 25 trading days with daily losses of at least -1% so far in 2026.
This includes 22 days with losses between -1% and -2%, 2 days between -2% and -3%, and 1 session with a decline of -3% or more.
7, or 28%, of these trading days occurred in October and November.
This compares with 29 such sessions in 2025 and 19 in 2024.

item.title: @wallstengine: $500B NVIDIA CHIP-FINANCING PLAN HAS DEPLOYED ZERO CAPITAL, WITH NO DEALS EXPECTED BEFORE 2027: WSJ...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$500B NVIDIA CHIP-FINANCING PLAN HAS DEPLOYED ZERO CAPITAL, WITH NO DEALS EXPECTED BEFORE 2027: WSJ
In August, $NVDA announced a partnership with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize $500B to help customers like OpenAI, Anthropic and smaller AI cloud companies finance chip purchases.
But the agreement was only a few-page memorandum of understanding. None of the firms was obligated to raise any money, and no capital has been deployed.
Jensen Huang had initially pushed for an even larger $1T financing program, partly to support Nvidia's valuation as its earnings grew but its valuation multiple declined.
He accelerated the effort after Apollo and Blackstone helped rival Broadcom arrange $35B in chip financing for Anthropic.
The biggest obstacle has been Nvidia's willingness to guarantee the loans:
Nvidia was willing to provide credit support covering up to 25% of project costs.
Broadcom provided residual-value guarantees covering about 85% of Anthropic's $35B Project Big Sky and just under 75% of its $63B Project North Star.
As lenders have become more cautious about AI financing, they have pushed Nvidia to offer greater protection.
Nvidia has also been pulling back its financial guarantees. Earlier, reports of a proposed $250B Nvidia backstop for an OpenAI data center sent $NVDA shares down 5%, prompting Nvidia to cut its initial commitment in half.
Interim CEO Colette Kress has since signaled that future investments and guarantees will be evaluated more strictly.
Talks on the partnership's first chip-backed financing deal are still underway, but nothing is expected to close before 2027.
Apollo CEO Marc Rowan warned that without Nvidia providing financial guarantees, a large number of neocloud companies could lose access to capital.

Jensen Huang had initially pushed for an even larger $1T financing program, partly to support Nvidia's valuation as its earnings grew but its valuation multiple declined.

He accelerated the effort after Apollo and Blackstone helped rival Broadcom arrange $35B in chip financing for Anthropic.

The biggest obstacle has been Nvidia's willingness to guarantee the loans:

Nvidia was willing to provide credit support covering up to 25% of project costs.

Broadcom provided residual-value guarantees covering about 85% of Anthropic's $35B Project Big Sky and just under 75% of its $63B Project North Star.

As lenders have become more cautious about AI financing, they have pushed Nvidia to offer greater protection.

Nvidia has also been pulling back its financial guarantees. Earlier, reports of a proposed $250B Nvidia backstop for an OpenAI data center sent $NVDA shares down 5%, prompting Nvidia to cut its initial commitment in half.

Interim CEO Colette Kress has since signaled that future investments and guarantees will be evaluated more strictly.

Talks on the partnership's first chip-backed financing deal are still underway, but nothing is expected to close before 2027.

item.title: @wallstengine: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on why the company offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees: The buyo...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on why the company offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees:
The buyouts were meant to give employees a sense of agency in making their own career choices.
Microsoft isn't treating software engineers as obsolete. Software engineering will "thrive," but the way teams are organized and the work engineers do will change significantly with AI.
Employees will increasingly become managers of AI agents and systems that produce the work, with this shift expected across all jobs.
One Microsoft team of just 11 developers building Cowork now builds "a software factory that builds the product," rather than building the product directly.
As a 51-year-old incumbent, Microsoft isn't an AI-first company. The transition to AI-driven workflows will take longer than many expect, and some employees may choose to leave.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Japan's exports jumped +20.5% YoY in October, to a record $74 billion, the 2nd-largest mo...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Japan's exports jumped +20.5% YoY in October, to a record $74 billion, the 2nd-largest monthly increase since October 2022.
Japan’s exports have now grown for 14 consecutive months, the longest streak since 2021-2023.
The surge was led by semiconductor manufacturing equipment shipments, which soared +49.7% YoY.
This was followed by electrical machinery exports, at +33.6% YoY growth, reflecting strong global investment in AI infrastructure.
Among regions, exports to Taiwan led with +42.7% YoY growth, followed by ASEAN at +34.7%, the US at +23.9%, the EU at +22.1%, and China at +13.3%.
Global chip demand is transforming the Japanese economy.

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC OFFICIALLY PRICES ITS IPO AT $83 A SHARE AT $1.49T VALUATION Anthropic $ANT sold 980 mill...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC OFFICIALLY PRICES ITS IPO AT $83 A SHARE AT $1.49T VALUATION
Anthropic $ANT sold 980 million shares to raise $81.34 billion, up from the 825 million it originally planned and above its $70-$78 range.
About $79.4 billion goes to Anthropic. Existing shareholders selling 23.6 million shares get about $2 billion.
Reuters calls it the biggest IPO ever, topping the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June before extra shares.
If underwriters buy all 147 million extra shares in their 30-day option, the raise would reach $93.5 billion, passing SpaceX's $85.7 billion total.
The price values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion fully diluted. With a $26 billion private placement from investors including Nvidia, Microsoft and Google, it will have more than $200 billion on its balance sheet, per the FT.
Shares start trading Thursday on Nasdaq.
item.content:encoded:
ANTHROPIC OFFICIALLY PRICES ITS IPO AT $83 A SHARE AT $1.49T VALUATION

Anthropic $ANT sold 980 million shares to raise $81.34 billion, up from the 825 million it originally planned and above its $70-$78 range.

About $79.4 billion goes to Anthropic. Existing shareholders selling 23.6 million shares get about $2 billion.

Reuters calls it the biggest IPO ever, topping the $75 billion SpaceX raised in June before extra shares.

If underwriters buy all 147 million extra shares in their 30-day option, the raise would reach $93.5 billion, passing SpaceX's $85.7 billion total.

The price values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion fully diluted. With a $26 billion private placement from investors including Nvidia, Microsoft and Google, it will have more than $200 billion on its balance sheet, per the FT.

Shares start trading Thursday on Nasdaq.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL LAUNCHES GEMINI 4 NEON
Google's new AI model is designed for complex coding, scientific research, analyzing docs and spreadsheets, and running AI agents that can complete multi-step tasks.
Beats Claude Opus 5.5 & GPT-6.2 Sol across several key benchmarks. Here's how they compare
(Neon / Opus 5.5 / GPT-6.2 Sol): AI Intelligence Index: 61 / 59 / 57 AutomationBench: 56.3% / 42.5% / 41.3% Advanced reasoning : 71.3% / 67.9% / 64.0% Science tasks: 70.5% / 63.3% / 68.0%
Neon ranks #3 overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, #1 on its Coding Agent Index, and #2 on the Vals Index and Agent Arena.
Google says Neon delivers a 32% lower cost per task than Gemini 4 Carbon at its default high thinking level.
Pricing: • Input: $3 per million tokens • Output: $15 per million tokens • Cached input: $0.15 per million tokens • Context window: 1 million tokens
It begins rolling out today through Gemini API, Google AI Studio and Gemini for business, as well as Google Antigravity and the Gemini app for paid Pro and Ultra subscribers.

BREAKING: Anthropic, $ANT, has priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its marketed range of $70 to $78, per Bloomberg.
The company is now expected to raise at least $68 billion through its IPO, plus another $26 billion in a private placement.
This brings the total offering to more than $94 billion, surpassing SpaceX’s record $86.2 billion IPO in June.
This marks the largest IPO in stock market history.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global fund managers cut their technology exposure by -25 percentage points in early Nove...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global fund managers cut their technology exposure by -25 percentage points in early November, to a net 12%, their biggest monthly decline since June 2006.
This marks even a larger monthly decline than during the 2022 bear market or the 2008 Financial Crisis.
As a result, technology is no longer the most overweight sector among fund managers.
The largest overweight positions are currently in Pharmaceuticals, at 34%, and Industrials, at 19%.
A record 38% of surveyed institutional investors believe companies are overinvesting, up from ~20% in January.
At the same time, 52% expect Big Tech companies to announce CapEx reductions over the next 6 months, up from 30% in October.
Institutional investors are rotating out of technology stocks at a rapid pace.

At the same time, 52% expect Big Tech companies to announce CapEx reductions over the next 6 months, up from 30% in October.

Institutional investors are rotating out of technology stocks at a rapid pace.

item.title: @wallstengine: JPMORGAN IS TRYING TO SELL $2B OF QUALTRICS DEBT AT A 20% DISCOUNT JPMorgan is marketing bonds tied...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
JPMORGAN IS TRYING TO SELL $2B OF QUALTRICS DEBT AT A 20% DISCOUNT
JPMorgan is marketing bonds tied to Qualtrics' $6.75B acquisition of Press Ganey Forsta at around 80 cents on the dollar, per FT.
The proposed terms: • Maturity: 6.5 years • Coupon: 8% • Issue price: 80 cents on the dollar • Implied yield: 12% to 13%
A group of banks, including JPMorgan, has been stuck holding more than $5B of acquisition debt since March after investors pulled back from software financing amid fears that AI could disrupt these businesses.
The banks had committed to providing the financing but couldn't sell the debt to outside investors, forcing them to fund the acquisition themselves.
JPMorgan is now trying to offload part of that debt before year-end, with the new bond sale expected to launch after Thanksgiving. Pricing is not yet final.
Qualtrics' existing term loan maturing in 2030 was also trading at around 82 cents on the dollar on Tuesday.
For comparison, cybersecurity firm Proofpoint just sold $2B of debt, including $1.25B in high-yield bonds that attracted more than $7B in orders and priced at an approximately 8.75% yield.

Why Nvidia Isn’t Going Up on Good Numbers
🔊
Nvidia ($NVDA) reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion after the bell yesterday. That’s more than double a year ago and above the $109.3 billion analysts expected.
It guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $130 billion, above estimates, and announced a $150 billion buyback. The stock was up about 3% premarket.

Nvidia’s past growth now becomes the base effect, Keith said. The faster a company grows, the harder that growth is to beat the next year.
He expects Nvidia’s revenue growth to peak in 2027, slow materially in the back half of that year, and fall to 30% to 40% in 2028.

item.title: @wallstengine: FED MINUTES FLAG RISKS IN THE AI BUILDOUT Most Fed officials noted that AI-related debt has grown r...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
FED MINUTES FLAG RISKS IN THE AI BUILDOUT
Most Fed officials noted that AI-related debt has grown rapidly, much of it through "complex and opaque" financing structures.
Fed staff warned that circular financing arrangements and off-balance-sheet lease commitments among AI firms could amplify losses if AI investment returns disappoint.
Several officials warned that the AI investment surge could be excessive, potentially leading to lower-than-expected returns.
Many officials viewed the AI buildout as a material source of inflation risk, with demand straining supply and pushing up prices, including beyond the data center industry.

item.description:
More details, per FT:
Aschenbrenner has held talks with Jefferies about opening a prime brokerage account. The bank previously turned him away over concerns that his fund was not adequately hedged.
Situational Awareness is also working with Clear Street and is looking to hire a chief risk officer.
Aschenbrenner has also discussed raising additional capital from outside investors next year, although the plans remain preliminary.
During the summer crisis, the fund sold most of its public holdings to Citadel at a discount to repay lenders, including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan. JPMorgan subsequently cut off lending.
The fund now has around 30 employees, compared with just eight disclosed in June.

item.title: @wallstengine: Leopold Aschenbrenner, 25, is looking to make a comeback in leveraged AI stock trading after his he...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Leopold Aschenbrenner, 25, is looking to make a comeback in leveraged AI stock trading after his hedge fund Situational Awareness nearly collapsed this summer.
The fund went from managing over $20B to needing an emergency rescue from Citadel within days after its AI bets went wrong.
It still manages over $10B, mostly in private investments, including a roughly $5B stake in Anthropic.
Despite pledging in July to stop borrowing, Aschenbrenner has discussed using leverage again and raising new capital. Neither plan is finalized.
Source: FT
item.content:encoded:
Leopold Aschenbrenner, 25, is looking to make a comeback in leveraged AI stock trading after his hedge fund Situational Awareness nearly collapsed this summer.

The fund went from managing over $20B to needing an emergency rescue from Citadel within days after its AI bets went wrong.

It still manages over $10B, mostly in private investments, including a roughly $5B stake in Anthropic.

Despite pledging in July to stop borrowing, Aschenbrenner has discussed using leverage again and raising new capital. Neither plan is finalized.

Source: FT

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI REPORTS UP TO 14% PPA IMPROVEMENT ON $AMD GPU DESIGNS OpenAI says its AI models rewrote Syst...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI REPORTS UP TO 14% PPA IMPROVEMENT ON $AMD GPU DESIGNS
OpenAI says its AI models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL for AMD's already heavily optimized flagship GPU IP, delivering roughly a year's worth of chip-design progress in less than 5 months.
The improvements involve power, performance and area (PPA), with several results already moving into production:
GPU: Up to 14% PPA improvement on flagship GPU IP.
Manufacturing: AMD has incorporated some AI-generated changes into a recent chip design sent for manufacturing, with others added to production design files for future versions.
CPU: AMD verified single-digit PPA improvements across key blocks of its upcoming next-generation flagship CPU.
OpenAI's Jalapeño chip: AI-assisted optimizations reduced standard-cell area by approximately 13% in its vector unit and 10% in its matrix unit, with the improvements verified on silicon.
OpenAI is also working with Synopsys to develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model designed to use professional chip-design and verification tools.

$MSFT is the FIRST company to announce plans to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging for its own Azure silicon.
EMIB connects multiple chiplets within a single package, allowing more flexible chip designs.
The new long-term agreement with Intel also secures multi-year Xeon CPU supply for Azure, including next-gen Diamond Rapids processors.
The companies will also expand work on CXL memory, Intel QuickAssist acceleration and TDX confidential computing, including encryption of VM memory and CPU state during host migrations.
Intel says its existing Azure optimizations deliver:
- Up to 2.3x greater performance and memory flexibility in Azure M-series v4 VMs using Xeon 6 and CXL memory.
- Up to 2.5x faster SQL backups through QuickAssist-enabled Azure VMs.
item.content:encoded:
MICROSOFT TO USE $INTC'S EMIB PACKAGING FOR AZURE CHIPS

$MSFT is the FIRST company to announce plans to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging for its own Azure silicon.

EMIB connects multiple chiplets within a single package, allowing more flexible chip designs.

The new long-term agreement with Intel also secures multi-year Xeon CPU supply for Azure, including next-gen Diamond Rapids processors.

The companies will also expand work on CXL memory, Intel QuickAssist acceleration and TDX confidential computing, including encryption of VM memory and CPU state during host migrations.

Intel says its existing Azure optimizations deliver:

- Up to 2.3x greater performance and memory flexibility in Azure M-series v4 VMs using Xeon 6 and CXL memory.

- Up to 2.5x faster SQL backups through QuickAssist-enabled Azure VMs.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Take a look at sentiment right now. Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are n...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Take a look at sentiment right now.
Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are now widespread calls that the "AI bubble has popped."
Sentiment is as though AI has failed, the investment wave is over, and we are in a global depression.
In reality? The S&P 500 is up +7% YTD, +60% in 5 years, and ~7% away from a record high, with US AI CapEx running at over $1 trillion per year.
Meanwhile, AI-associated sectors and tech investments have accounted for ~44% of total US GDP growth on a rolling four-quarter basis.
And, Nvidia, $NVDA, is guiding nearly $750 billion in revenue for next year, even without Jensen Huang.
The underlying fundamentals of the AI Revolution have not suddenly deteriorated because of a leadership crisis at one company.
The unfortunate result of this drawdown, as with nearly every other correction since the AI Revolution began, will be countless investors getting crushed on the way back up.
Today's fearmongers become tomorrow's short squeeze as soon as sentiment shifts again.
The comments on this post will be a perfect example of just how polarized sentiment has become in the "doom" direction.
Asset owners will win and the AI Revolution is far from over.
item.content:encoded:
Take a look at sentiment right now.

Because of a personal event involving Jensen Huang, there are now widespread calls that the "AI bubble has popped."

Sentiment is as though AI has failed, the investment wave is over, and we are in a global depression.

In reality? The S&P 500 is up +7% YTD, +60% in 5 years, and ~7% away from a record high, with US AI CapEx running at over $1 trillion per year.

Meanwhile, AI-associated sectors and tech investments have accounted for ~44% of total US GDP growth on a rolling four-quarter basis.

And, Nvidia, $NVDA, is guiding nearly $750 billion in revenue for next year, even without Jensen Huang.

The underlying fundamentals of the AI Revolution have not suddenly deteriorated because of a leadership crisis at one company.

The unfortunate result of this drawdown, as with nearly every other correction since the AI Revolution began, will be countless investors getting crushed on the way back up.

Today's fearmongers become tomorrow's short squeeze as soon as sentiment shifts again.

The comments on this post will be a perfect example of just how polarized sentiment has become in the "doom" direction.

Asset owners will win and the AI Revolution is far from over.

item.title: @wallstengine: CodeRabbit just launched Verify in public beta, an AI QA agent that tests whether code changes actu...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
CodeRabbit just launched Verify in public beta, an AI QA agent that tests whether code changes actually work in a running application.
It analyzes pull requests, generates test scenarios, and runs user journeys in a browser to check whether the application behaves as intended.
When it finds a bug, it captures screenshots, session recordings, and logs so developers can see exactly what went wrong.
Here's an example from the demo:
A customer applies a SAVE20 coupon to a $100 order. The checkout correctly displays an $80 total, but the simulated charge still shows $100.
CodeRabbit Verify catches the discrepancy and provides the evidence needed to reproduce it.
Developers can then send those findings directly to CodeRabbit Agent or their preferred coding agent to implement a fix.
Testing is free during the public beta

item.title: @wallstengine: Microsoft $MSFT is nearing a deal to sell TikTok parent ByteDance an additional $500M in Azure AI s...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Microsoft $MSFT is nearing a deal to sell TikTok parent ByteDance an additional $500M in Azure AI services, primarily for access to OpenAI models.
The potential deal is creating tensions with OpenAI, which has raised concerns that Chinese companies could use its models to train competing AI through distillation.
Microsoft says it has found no evidence that ByteDance is doing so and believes the company primarily uses the models for software development.
ByteDance was already on track to spend roughly $1B annually on Microsoft's AI and cloud services as of June, excluding this potential deal.
While OpenAI restricts direct access for most Chinese companies, Microsoft's licensing rights allow it to sell OpenAI models through Azure to Chinese customers.
Source: The Information
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft $MSFT is nearing a deal to sell TikTok parent ByteDance an additional $500M in Azure AI services, primarily for access to OpenAI models.

The potential deal is creating tensions with OpenAI, which has raised concerns that Chinese companies could use its models to train competing AI through distillation.

Microsoft says it has found no evidence that ByteDance is doing so and believes the company primarily uses the models for software development.

ByteDance was already on track to spend roughly $1B annually on Microsoft's AI and cloud services as of June, excluding this potential deal.

While OpenAI restricts direct access for most Chinese companies, Microsoft's licensing rights allow it to sell OpenAI models through Azure to Chinese customers.

Source: The Information

item.title: @wallstengine: Here's what Wall Street says about $NVDA after its first earnings since Jensen's exit: Q3 beat, Q4...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Here's what Wall Street says about $NVDA after its first earnings since Jensen's exit:
Q3 beat, Q4 guidance topped estimates, FY28 growth raised to 75%, and Jensen's return ruled out.
1. UBS (Buy, $220 PT, cut from $240)
"This should help a little in the near term as some investors have been worried about C2027 cuts, but our view has always been that this is more about how much things decelerate in C2028. On one hand, it would have been nice to see C2028 supply commits increase significantly as well, but on the other hand, we think there is a very real risk that NVDA becomes beholden to these purchase commitments and has to keep throwing money at its customers to drive revenue."
"Lastly, the company announced that the 10-Q will be filed 'in the coming weeks' - later than usual. When queried on our callback, management indicated this was related to the ongoing investigation and whether any additional risk factors would need to be added to the filing."
2. Jefferies (Buy, $250 PT, cut from $300)
"Management noted that cloud industry backlog reached $2.5 trillion, up from $2 trillion three months ago, while Hopper GPUs have recontracted at up to twice their original price and B300 rental rates have increased more than 60% since introduction. In our view, higher rental rates across GPU generations provide tangible evidence that available supply remains well below demand."
"At the same time, we believe the durability of the growth trajectory remains closely linked to spending from leading AI labs and continued evidence of AI ROI, factors largely outside of NVDA’s control."
3. Susquehanna (Positive, $275 PT)
"That said, revenues in the quarter included ~$2.4B of Hopper sales to China that were not previously included in the companys CY3Q guidance. Additionally, there was a 14th week to be included in the fourth quarter."
"To meet its outsized growth expectations, the company increased its supply commitment by roughly ~$110B (now ~$390B), with investments mostly centered on securing additional HBM capacity."
4. Stifel (Buy, $205 PT)
"Three takes for our coverage: (1) NVIDIA’s capital is pivoting from customer financing toward supplier prepayments, positive for substrate, packaging, EMS and optical capacity; (2) networking above $21B with CPO in volume production broadens optical content; and (3) with FY28 growth capped by supply rather than demand, unmet demand creates an opening for second sources."
5. Morgan Stanley (Overweight, $260 PT, cut from $267)
"But given the uncertainty with respect to Commerce Department actions, reports of DOJ and SEC investigations, as well as Nvidia’s own internal investigation related to the CEO transition, we considered it a strong possibility Nvidia would not provide any updates to its prior FY28 guidance."
"However, Nvidia proceeded to raise its guide for FY28 revenue growth from 70% to 75%, and on a higher FY27 base that translates to an incremental $50bn or so in revenues next year vs. the prior outlook."
"We continue to take a more cautious view than management with respect to 2027 revenue growth, raising our estimates from 52% to 56% y/y growth."
6. Truist Securities (Hold, $174 PT)
"Despite solid results & outlook, we see more questions than answers; Management says 'We got this,' but it's just not that easy."
"Unfortunately, the most challenging questions were not asked on the call. Specifically: (1) How much revenue might new Dept of Commerce rules curtail? (2) What will be the effect of the political power shift in the U.S. on land/power/shell availability in the coming 1-2 years? and (3) What's the status of the CEO direct report engagement?"
7. Yorkville Ives (Outperform, $225 PT)
"Kress said Nvidia will continue to be disciplined and selective and is rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees as additional sources of capital become available: land, power, and shell is the top priority for any future support, investment-grade customers are where prepayment arrangements would be considered, guarantees start only once a neocloud has secured its financing and the capacity is deployed and accepted, and capital goes to suppliers and the buyback first."
8. Melius Research (Hold, $185 PT)
"You could say the extra week in F4Q27 accounts for about $9-10B of the ~$14B q/q increase guided for in the quarter, versus the ~$20B of q/q growth in F3Q27, but guidance did come in ~$5B above consensus."
"The real surprising statement was then to go ahead and raise FY28 growth by 500bps (about $45B in revenue after beat and raise in F2H27). FY28 is when you'd think the sales to countries cited in new BIS restrictions would tank and some capital shortages would hurt growth in neoclouds. The 75% statement indicates that hyperscalers will take whatever they can get."
9. Aletheia Capital (Hold)
"However, off-balance sheet commitments surged by nearly $60bn QoQ to $224bn as NVDA continues to provide backstops to neoclouds and AI infrastructure guarantees to other customers, while multiple federal and regulatory investigations remain an overhang on the stock."
"Although shares trade at an undemanding valuation, we remain on the sidelines until there is greater clarity around its earnings outlook and the strategic direction set by the incoming CEO."
10. Cantor Fitzgerald (Overweight, $250 PT)
"We note the updated CY27 revenue guide includes zero contributions from China as well as reflects the company’s initial work toward the recent BIS rules banning sales to SE Asian Cloud providers."
"Bigger picture, clear questions remain around talent retention, customer engagement, supply chain management, and extreme co-design for products beyond Feynman, but today’s call was well executed."
"We highlight a robust team of 42,000 employees that will execute the 2027-2028 roadmap across Rubin Ultra and Feynman, in what we believe will be a sustained compute-constrained world."
11. Bank of America (Buy, $280 PT)
"Meanwhile, valuation at <10x CY27E PE (vs. 30x median) indicates perhaps the most compelling risk reward across our coverage."
"Our base case is for FY29/CY28E ~30% sales and 35% YoY pf-EPS growth towards $23.17, or implied 6.6x PE. In a bear-case scenario of zero sales growth YoY, NVDA could still generate ~$16 in pf-EPS or 9.7x implied PE."
"If we assume more robust 40%+ YoY in a bull-case scenario, NVDA could generate close to $26.59."
12. Wells Fargo (Overweight, $250 PT, cut from $300)
"We would again highlight purchase commit expansion to $390B exiting F2Q27 (+$111B q/q); total inventory + purchase commits at $429.7B (+$119B q/q)."
"Management reit. confidence / no change in Neocloud commits ($32B, -$4B q/q), w/ power and systems credit support guarantees at $9.5B; Neocloud land, power, & shell guarantees at $3.5B."
13. JPMorgan (Overweight, $230 PT, raised from $215)
"More importantly (and rather surprisingly), the company raised its FY28 revenue growth outlook, with the team now guiding for ~75% Y/Y growth (up from ~70% prior) off what is now a higher FY27 base, citing both sustained demand and incremental supply support from its partners (this implies total revs could reach ~$741B in FY28, ~6% above consensus estimates)."
"Strength in the quarter itself was primarily driven by the Vera Rubin ramp, which added ~$20B of revenue in its first full quarter of shipments (fastest product ramp in NVDAs history)."
14. Barclays (Overweight, $210 PT)
"However, the company didnt go so far as to explicitly comment on China's indirect access through SE Asia and that will remain an overhang into CY27."
"On the fundamental side, GMs are probably the most positive surprise at nearly 100bps higher vs. St. in the reported quarter due to better product mix with more Blackwell Ultra than expected, despite the initial Rubin ramp ($20B in FQ3)."
"Consistent messaging on demand and support of the ecosystem has us walking away feeling more positive, but the decision around leadership remains in limbo."
15. Summit Insights (Downgraded to Hold from Buy)
"We are downgrading NVDA to a hold because we believe the leadership change creates uncertainty around NVDA's roadmap beyond Vera Rubin."
"We are concerned that the Department of Commerce’s ruling can cause unintended negative consequences for NVDA and the broader AI ecosystem in 2027."
"We expect custom ASICs to gain share against NVDA in 2027 as supply chain capacity frees up."
16. Piper Sandler (Overweight, $230 PT, cut from $300)
"Following results, we lift FY27-28E EPS 5/9%, but lower our PT to $230 on a ~10x CY28E PE multiple (vs 14x) due to uncertainty around the CEO transition."
"The stock may remain range bound until clarity on the new CEO emerges, however we see current trough multiple of ~10x CY27E $16 EPS as a buying opportunity for long term investors."
17. DA Davidson (Buy, $200 PT)
"Results came in above expectations, with revenue beating consensus by ~6%, driven in large part by the hyperscaler segment growing 23.5% sequentially to $60B (13.5% above consensus). Management attributed the hyperscaler outperformance to the ramp of Vera Rubin."
"AI Clouds, Industrial, and Enterprise (ACIE) came in at $47.5B, growing ~18% sequentially and ~127.5% Y/Y, however missing estimates by ~3%."
18. HSBC (Hold, $170 PT)
"Earnings beat and revisions were not the focus as investors wanted to see management instil confidence not only in NVIDIA but overall AI trade given Jensen Huang’s departure."
"However, we see limited room for any significant valuation re rating until 1) a permanent succession plan is laid out; and 2) the new leadership demonstrates execution capability to deliver the product roadmap."
19. RBC Capital (Outperform, $230 PT)
"We raise estimates and at ~9x CY27 EPS, we see attractive risk/reward despite the CEO transition given: 1) demand is significantly outpacing supply; 2) product roadmap is set for next 3 years; and 3) industry supply tightness should limit NT competitive risk."
20. KeyBanc (Sector Weight)
"Additionally, NVDA clarified its $32B in Neoclouds obligations would only backstop customers who have secured financing, otherwise its commits could be reduced/eliminated. NVDA said it is no longer shipping H200 to China."
"We remain SW, as uncertainty regarding who Jensen's successor will be likely keeps the stock range-bound."
21. Goldman Sachs (Buy, $220 PT)
"First, Nvidia raised its CY27 revenue growth forecast to 75% from 70%, even after accounting for the impact of newly-issued US Department of Commerce restrictions on datacenter rentals by Nvidia's customers to restricted geographies, including mainland China."
"Second, Nvidia reiterated its commitment to financial guarantees and commitments for both partners and customers, including neoclouds - and noted that this support will continue in a disciplined and selective manner."
22. Mizuho (Outperform, $220 PT)
"Key points: 1) F28E raised to up 75% y/y to ~$742B (prior ~$700B), with unlocked supply, and Vera CPU revs >2x y/y, 2) F28E GM target holding at 72.5% (in line w/cons.), despite pricing pressure concerns."
"Even assuming China restrictions (Exhibit 3), share loss, and significant GM contraction, we see nearly 40% upside."
23. Needham (Buy, $200 PT)
"The company addressed future financing commitments and will remain disciplined and selective when it comes to new deals to support neoclouds and other AI partners."
"Management expects F4Q27 to mark the gross margin trough and guided FY28 to 72%-73% as higher ASP Rubin platforms become a larger part of the mix."
24. Wedbush (Outperform, $293 PT, raised from $275)
"Specifically, with or without Jensen, NVDA's near to intermediate-term demand profile has not changed as exemplified by another beat and raise and management's confidence in raising the FY2028 growth outlook (to 75% from 70%)."
"Net, with NVDA trading below 10X our FY2028 EPS estimates and at just 14X annualized FQ4'27 earnings, we believe worse than worst case scenarios are already baked into investor expectations."

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US household stock market holdings are on track for a record $9 trillion annual gain in 2...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US household stock market holdings are on track for a record $9 trillion annual gain in 2026, according to BofA estimates.
Since January 2025, household equity holdings have surged +$19 trillion, to a record $75 trillion.
This comes as the S&P 500 has rallied +26%, while the Nasdaq 100 has risen +29% over this period.
Since 2020, US household stock market holdings are up +$50 trillion, or +200%.
With consumer spending accounting for ~70% of US GDP, strong stock market gains continue to support the broader economy.
Asset owners are winning.

item.title: @wallstengine: Mass production of displays for Apple's $AAPL iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 largely won't begin until...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Mass production of displays for Apple's $AAPL iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 largely won't begin until January, ahead of an expected March 2027 launch.
The reason is that display manufacturers are prioritizing the higher-value iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and Duo models through the end of 2026. The standard and Air models require fewer, less complex panels, allowing production to start later.
Apple is also reportedly planning lower production volumes for the iPhone Air 2 following weak demand for the original model.
Samsung is expected to be the sole display supplier for the Air 2, while Samsung and LG Display will split orders for the standard iPhone 18.
Source: AppleInsider

item.title: @wallstengine: SpaceX's $40B AI chip financing could begin selling to investors as soon as this week, with the deb...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
SpaceX's $40B AI chip financing could begin selling to investors as soon as this week, with the debt structured to stay off the company's balance sheet, according to Semafor.
The financing will run through a special-purpose vehicle (SPV), allowing $SPCX to lease the GPUs without directly carrying the debt.
Apollo is expected to lend nearly $20B upfront before selling or syndicating the debt to other investors.
Of the seven financing tranches, $35.5B is expected to carry interest rates of 7.75% and 8.3%, while riskier portions totaling less than $3B could cost over 9%.

item.description:
Some on Twitter often ask me why @hedgeye @KeithMcCullough is my only outside research source that my hedge fund @seabreezelp pays for.
I have explained, in the past, that the muti-decade transformation from active (dominated by "stock pickers") to passive management (governed by machines/algos and products and strategies that 'worship at the altar of price momentum") requires quantitative input (Fractals/The Mandlebrot Set) to complement our fundamental research and analysis. (As well, @hedgeye large research department generates great ideas to follow up on (e.g $MPT).
Though many are critical of his delivery and his "us v them" attitude - that is necessary because the establishment (business media, sell side) is filled with the foul odor of "Group Stink" and herdlike behavior that doesn't timestamp and exhibit analytical rigor/process. Moreover, being an independent research source is a threat to the consensus Sell Side and compromised "talking heads" on Fin TV (who have cost viewers dearly with their poorly researched investment "ideas" that are exposed when "the tide goes out? (I recently compared the hurdles to @hedgeye ascent as a value added independent research source to that of my famous sister's (Deborah Kass) remarkable rise as a prominent artist (beginning in the male dominated artist community of the 1970s-1990s period).
Which gets me to another unbelievably good call from the guys in Stamford Ctr. -- to avoid/short silver and gold - a truly contrarian view.
Just look at the chart of silver and gold in the last few months and the further decline today (GLD -$7 or -2% and SLV down by another three percent).
Keith McCullough on X: "BREAKING: Gold's Crash is now at -30% from its #Quad1 Cycle Peak https://twitter.com/KeithMcCullough/status/2123001648024780950/photo/1" / X
Well, those sort of calls are "as good as gold."
If you respect your hard earned capital, I suggest you look into subscribing to @hedgeye.
I do.
@KeithMcCullough @Hedgeye_HGRO @RPKInvestor @HedgeyeDJ

Nvidia's dominance in the global data center chip market is unprecedented:
Nvidia accounted for 76% of global server GPU revenue in Q4 2025.
This is more than 3 times the combined revenue of all its competitors.
Broadcom, $AVGO, came next, accounting for 10% of the market.
By comparison, AMD, $AMD, represented just 3% of total revenue.
This comes as Nvidia has spent years investing in GPU applications beyond gaming, long before the AI boom.
Nvidia is firmly in control of the AI chip market.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US margin debt fell -$32 billion in October amid the market's selloff, to $1.45 trillion,...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US margin debt fell -$32 billion in October amid the market's selloff, to $1.45 trillion, but remains at its 4th-highest level on record.
This follows a combined +$63 billion increase in September and August, and a -$85 billion drop in July.
Year-to-date, margin debt has surged +$223 billion, or +18%.
Since the 2022 bear market low, this metric is up +$842 billion, or +139%.
As a % of M2 money supply, margin debt now stands at 6.2%, its 3rd-highest reading since the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble of 6.4%.
Despite recent volatility, this market remains highly levered.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA's future commitments climbed to $518B, from $366B last quarter. Separately, Nvidia disclosed...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA's future commitments climbed to $518B, from $366B last quarter.
Separately, Nvidia disclosed $32B in conditional neocloud agreements, down from $36B.
Here's the breakdown of the $518B: > Supply and capacity: $390B (vs. $279B), largely multi-year memory purchases > Cloud services & data center leases: $102B (vs. $54B) > Equity investments: $20B (vs. $25B) > Capital expenditures: $6B (vs. $8B)
The additional $32B in neocloud commitments only takes effect if partners secure financing and the compute capacity is deployed, operational, and accepted by Nvidia.
item.content:encoded:
$NVDA's future commitments climbed to $518B, from $366B last quarter.

Separately, Nvidia disclosed $32B in conditional neocloud agreements, down from $36B.

Here's the breakdown of the $518B:
> Supply and capacity: $390B (vs. $279B), largely multi-year memory purchases
> Cloud services & data center leases: $102B (vs. $54B)
> Equity investments: $20B (vs. $25B)
> Capital expenditures: $6B (vs. $8B)

The additional $32B in neocloud commitments only takes effect if partners secure financing and the compute capacity is deployed, operational, and accepted by Nvidia.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
To all of the recent AI doubters:
Nvidia's, $NVDA, earnings just proved that the AI buildout is far from over.
In fact, it is accelerating beyond already elevated expectations.
The company generated $1.3 billion in revenue per day last quarter and is now guiding for $130 billion in revenue next quarter.
Revenue and adjusted EPS surged +103% and +106% year-over-year, respectively.
Data center revenue jumped +110%, while the company expanded its share buybacks by another +$150 billion.
This is a $4 trillion company growing at the pace of an explosive startup.
Even amid unprecedented leadership uncertainty and mounting skepticism surrounding CapEx, the underlying fundamentals of the AI infrastructure buildout remain exceptionally strong.
We are in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in history.
The AI buildout is not slowing down. It is accelerating.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI is transforming Japan's economy: The Sentiment Index for Japanese manufacturers rose +5 points i...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI is transforming Japan's economy:
The Sentiment Index for Japanese manufacturers rose +5 points in November, to 27, the highest level since August 2021.
This marks the 4th consecutive monthly increase, totaling +14 points.
Excluding August 2021, this is the strongest sentiment among Japanese manufacturers in 8 years.
The Electronics Sector Index alone surged +14 points, to 39, driven by rising memory chip demand.
At the same time, the Precision Machinery Index increased +4 points, to 42, supported by strong domestic and international orders.
Meanwhile, the sentiment among non-manufacturers surged +12 points in November, to 35, the highest level since June 2018.
AI investment is boosting business confidence across Japan.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
MICROSOFT ANNOUNCES 6 NEW AI MODELS AT IGNITE
$MSFT unveiled six MAI models across coding, cybersecurity, image generation and voice on the same day its partner OpenAI released GPT-6.2.
1) MAI Code 2: Delivers 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the cost. Now in GitHub Copilot.
2) MAI Code 2 Flash: Outperformed GPT-6.1 Sol in AT&T testing while costing 50 times less.
3) MAI Cyber 2 Flash: Outperformed GPT-6 Astra on a cybersecurity benchmark at less than 2% of the cost per task.
4) MAI Realtime 1: Outperformed GPT Realtime 2.1 on public benchmarks and Microsoft's own evaluations.
Microsoft is also launching MAI Image 2.7 in public preview and bringing MAI Transcribe 2 to Dragon Copilot for medical use cases.
Separately, Microsoft says it is making progress on its own general-purpose frontier AI model.

1) MAI Code 2: Delivers 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the cost. Now in GitHub Copilot.

2) MAI Code 2 Flash: Outperformed GPT-6.1 Sol in AT&T testing while costing 50 times less.

4) MAI Realtime 1: Outperformed GPT Realtime 2.1 on public benchmarks and Microsoft's own evaluations.

item.title: @wallstengine: GENESIS AI RAISES $500M AT A $3.5 BILLION VALUATION The robotics startup is building Eno, a wheeled...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
GENESIS AI RAISES $500M AT A $3.5 BILLION VALUATION
The robotics startup is building Eno, a wheeled robot with two dexterous hands designed to perform physical tasks in factories, warehouses and laboratories.
What makes its approach interesting is how it trains the robot.
People wear sensor-equipped gloves and cameras while performing real-world tasks. The gloves record finger movements, touch and force, teaching its GENE AI model not just how to pick up objects, but how much pressure to apply when handling them.
More than 100 workers are already helping collect this training data, according to TechCrunch.
Genesis is developing its AI model alongside its own physics simulator and robotic hands, with manufacturing and logistics as its first target markets. https://x.com/zhou_xian_/status/2122752003197833357/video/1

item.title: @wallstengine: ANTHROPIC EXPECTS TO PRICE ITS IPO ABOVE $80 PER SHARE: WSJ The Claude maker originally targeted $7...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ANTHROPIC EXPECTS TO PRICE ITS IPO ABOVE $80 PER SHARE: WSJ
The Claude maker originally targeted $70-$78 per share, but its advisers are now discussing a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion, up from roughly $1.33 trillion at the initial range.
Hedge funds have placed unusually large orders, with Altimeter founder Brad Gerstner saying his firm requested $5 billion worth of shares.
Existing investors, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures and Accel, also reportedly plan to increase their investments rather than sell down their stakes.
At the original price range, Anthropic planned to sell around $61 billion in IPO shares, alongside a separate $26 billion private placement backed by investors including Google and Nvidia. The company also plans to allocate up to 20% of the IPO to retail investors.
Final pricing is expected Wednesday, with trading set to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq under $ANT.
item.content:encoded:
ANTHROPIC EXPECTS TO PRICE ITS IPO ABOVE $80 PER SHARE: WSJ

The Claude maker originally targeted $70-$78 per share, but its advisers are now discussing a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion, up from roughly $1.33 trillion at the initial range.

Hedge funds have placed unusually large orders, with Altimeter founder Brad Gerstner saying his firm requested $5 billion worth of shares.

Existing investors, including Bessemer Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures and Accel, also reportedly plan to increase their investments rather than sell down their stakes.

At the original price range, Anthropic planned to sell around $61 billion in IPO shares, alongside a separate $26 billion private placement backed by investors including Google and Nvidia. The company also plans to allocate up to 20% of the IPO to retail investors.

Final pricing is expected Wednesday, with trading set to begin Thursday on the Nasdaq under $ANT.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Nvidia's board should act now.
We believe Jensen Huang's newly released statement is only further evidence that he resigned from his position as CEO of Nvidia, $NVDA, in the heat of the moment.
Today, Jensen made it clear that he is willing to return, calling it an "honor" to answer calls for him to return as CEO.
Nvidia's board should now acknowledge, at the very least, that pending the results of the independent investigation, the door for Jensen to return has not closed.
Preserving this option is not a commitment to reinstatement, but rather an acknowledgment that the board's ultimate decision should be guided by the findings of the investigation and the long-term interests of shareholders.
If not, shareholders must act.

item.title: @wallstengine: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has issued a statement ahead of the company's first earnings call wi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has issued a statement ahead of the company's first earnings call without him, signaling his willingness to return if the board asks:
“Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me.
I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor.
Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA.
I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.
Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company.
If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.
Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours.”

item.title: @wallstengine: AN AI MODEL IDENTIFIED A SCHOOL IN IRAN AS A MILITARY TARGET IN 22 OF 32 SIMULATED TESTS. An indepe...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
AN AI MODEL IDENTIFIED A SCHOOL IN IRAN AS A MILITARY TARGET IN 22 OF 32 SIMULATED TESTS.
An independent investigation by Vals, reported by Bloomberg, tested AI models from eight companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and DeepSeek, to examine how they performed in simulated military-targeting scenarios.
Researchers found that models sometimes identified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers and schools as military targets.
One of the most concerning findings came from satellite imagery of Minab, Iran, which included a school that was later hit in a deadly strike earlier this year.
Here's what researchers found:
• Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 identified the school as a military target in 22 of 32 tests.
• When researchers described the scenario as a game, Claude selected the school 23 of 32 times.
• OpenAI models avoided selecting the school in the initial tests. But when told the scenario was a game, three models selected it 9, 11 and 13 times, respectively.
In a separate set of nearly 400 simulated drone-targeting tests, researchers found that some models continued identifying civilians as military targets even after imagery showed people being wounded or killed.
Researchers also found that relatively simple prompts, such as telling the models not to overthink safety or presenting scenarios as games, could make them more willing to identify civilian targets.
Anthropic acknowledged that these scenarios violate its policies and said current AI systems are not reliable enough to operate fully autonomous weapons. OpenAI and Google also said their policies prohibit such uses.
These were simplified simulations involving commercially available AI models, not actual military operations. The study did not examine military targeting procedures, legal reviews, human oversight or specialized government AI systems.

US corporate earnings remain remarkably strong.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: It's officially Nvidia's earnings day. Today's earnings report and call will likely be the most wat...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
It's officially Nvidia's earnings day.
Today's earnings report and call will likely be the most watched earnings event in history.
We are watching two key things:
1. Do executives show any willingness to reinstate Jensen Huang
2. What has CHANGED from a business perspective
As of now, considering the information over the last 48 hours, we believe there is an <20% chance that Jensen returns.
Any indication that the probability is higher would be strongly bullish for the stock.
But, if not, then what has changed for Nvidia? With or without Jensen, this company remains one of the best businesses in the world.
We are looking to see if the company still expects revenue growth of 70%+ in FY2028, as management previously indicated.
We also look for any changes to AI infrastructure spending, demand for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips, and the company's relationships with its largest customers.
If the fundamental outlook remains intact, then investors must ask: Does Jensen Huang's departure justify the -$750 billion in lost market cap?
We believe the market has already priced in a significant portion of the uncertainty surrounding Jensen's departure.
At the same time, the long-term AI infrastructure investment cycle remains intact, and Nvidia continues to sit at the center of it.
The burden is now on management to demonstrate that the business can continue executing at the same level without Jensen Huang.
More to come after earnings.

But, if not, then what has changed for Nvidia? With or without Jensen, this company remains one of the best businesses in the world.

We also look for any changes to AI infrastructure spending, demand for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips, and the company's relationships with its largest customers.

If the fundamental outlook remains intact, then investors must ask: Does Jensen Huang's departure justify the -$750 billion in lost market cap?

We believe the market has already priced in a significant portion of the uncertainty surrounding Jensen's departure.

At the same time, the long-term AI infrastructure investment cycle remains intact, and Nvidia continues to sit at the center of it.

The burden is now on management to demonstrate that the business can continue executing at the same level without Jensen Huang.

More to come after earnings.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Essential expenses are taking up an increasing portion of US household spending: Healthcare, housin...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Essential expenses are taking up an increasing portion of US household spending:
Healthcare, housing, utilities, gasoline, financial services, and insurance now account for 45.6% of total US consumer expenditures, near the highest proportion on record.
Over the last 4 years, this figure has risen +1.8 percentage points from its lowest level since 2004.
By comparison, these essential expenses represented a record 46.5% in 2010, following the 2008 Financial Crisis.
Meanwhile, between the 1960s and the 1980s, this proportion never exceeded 40%.
In 1959, these categories accounted for less than 30% of total consumer expenditures.
Mandatory spending is eating up a growing portion of US household budgets.

item.description:
BREAKING: Interest expense on US Federal debt surged +$11 billion YoY in October, to $115 billion, its highest October reading on record.
This marks the 2nd consecutive YoY increase, totaling +$33 billion.
Interest expense in October has surged +$96 billion since 2022, or +505%.
As a result, interest payments accounted for 31.3% of total government outlays last month, the highest proportion on record.
This figure has more than quadrupled over the last 4 years.
The cost of US debt is surging at an alarming rate.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US hiring plans are picking up as seasonal demand accelerates: US-based employers announced plans t...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US hiring plans are picking up as seasonal demand accelerates:
US-based employers announced plans to hire 444,692 workers in October, up +57% YoY and the highest October total since at least 2009.
Technology led with 300,252 announced positions, followed by Transportation at 100,000, and Retail at 13,300.
Year-to-date hiring plans are up +34% YoY, to 655,304 workers.
Meanwhile, seasonal hiring announcements jumped +26% YoY, to 470,400, but remained 29% below the 660,150 recorded in 2024.
Seasonal positions now account for 72% of all hiring plans in 2026 and nearly 60% of the increase from last year.
Seasonal hiring is gaining momentum.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Value stocks are making a historic comeback: The Russell 1000 Value Index is outperforming the Russ...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Value stocks are making a historic comeback:
The Russell 1000 Value Index is outperforming the Russell 1000 Growth Index by 27.7 percentage points so far in 2026, its strongest relative performance since 2000.
The Russell 1000 Value Index includes stocks across multiple sectors, including healthcare, industrials, consumer staples, and utilities.
This marks a sharp reversal after growth stocks outperformed value by 31.2 percentage points in 2023, 19.0 percentage points in 2024, and 2.7 percentage points in 2025.
By comparison, during the 2022 bear market, value stocks outperformed growth by 21.6 percentage points.
This comes as the Russell 1000 Value Index is up +24.8% year-to-date, while the Russell 1000 Growth Index is down -2.9% over the same period.
Market dynamics are rapidly shifting.
