item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors are demanding more compensation for holding US tech debt: US investment-grade (IG) techno...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors are demanding more compensation for holding US tech debt:
US investment-grade (IG) technology bonds are underperforming the broader IG corporate bond market by -9% year-to-date.
This brings the total return of IG tech bonds relative to broader IG bonds down to its lowest level in at least 30 years.
At the same time, the difference between IG technology bond spreads over Treasuries and broader IG corporate bond spreads over Treasuries has widened to +15 basis points, the widest in at least 14 years.
By comparison, this difference was negative from 2012 through 2025.
In other words, investors are demanding a higher yield premium to hold technology debt than the broader IG corporate bond market.
This comes as Big Tech bond issuance has surged to a record $182 billion so far in 2026, up +971% from just $17 billion in 2024, making AI the largest sector in the IG bond market.
Financing the AI revolution is becoming more expensive.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Tons of US car owners owe more on their vehicles than they are worth: 29% of trade-ins for new-vehi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Tons of US car owners owe more on their vehicles than they are worth:
29% of trade-ins for new-vehicle purchases involved negative equity in Q3 2026, near the highest proportion since Q1 2021.
At the same time, the average amount owed on underwater vehicles rose to $7,107, the 3rd-highest on record.
This is +$2,960 above the low recorded in Q4 2021 and +$1,850 above pre-pandemic levels.
Meanwhile, buyers who rolled over unpaid car debt into new loans took on an average loan balance of $57,235, up +44% from 2019.
The average annual percentage rate (APR) for these borrowers was 8.1%, pushing total interest payments over the life of their loans to $16,610, up +83% from $9,093 in 2019.
The US is in a car affordability crisis.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US Social Security Trust Fund’s deficit jumped +$39 billion YoY in Fiscal Year 2026,...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US Social Security Trust Fund’s deficit jumped +$39 billion YoY in Fiscal Year 2026, to a record -$221 billion.
This fund finances retirement benefits and payments to eligible survivors of deceased workers.
This comes as the fund’s costs, primarily benefit payments to retirees and survivors, soared +$83 billion YoY, to $1.5 trillion, an all-time high.
At the same time, income, primarily from contributions to the Social Security system, rose +$44 billion YoY, to a record $1.3 trillion.
Since FY2022, the fund’s deficit has surged +$188 billion, or +585%.
As a result, trust fund reserves fell -$221 billion YoY in FY2026, to $2.18 trillion, the lowest since 2007, down down -$640 billion from the 2017 peak.
The financial health of Social Security is deteriorating rapidly.

At the same time, income, primarily from contributions to the Social Security system, rose +$44 billion YoY, to a record $1.3 trillion.

Since FY2022, the fund’s deficit has surged +$188 billion, or +585%.

As a result, trust fund reserves fell -$221 billion YoY in FY2026, to $2.18 trillion, the lowest since 2007, down down -$640 billion from the 2017 peak.

The financial health of Social Security is deteriorating rapidly.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Businesses using AI are far more optimistic about their growth: Among US firms using AI, the share...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Businesses using AI are far more optimistic about their growth:
Among US firms using AI, the share expecting revenue to increase over the next 12 months exceeds the share expecting a decrease by 48.2 percentage points, according to the Federal Reserve Banks' 2025 Small Business Credit Survey.
By comparison, this gap is just 20.6 percentage points among firms not using AI, less than half the figure for AI adopters.
At the same time, the share of AI-using firms expecting employment to increase exceeds the share expecting a decrease by 32.7 percentage points, compared to just 15.2 percentage points among non-adopters.
These differences persist even after accounting for firm characteristics, business-owner demographics, and changes in revenue and employment over the previous 12 months.
After adjusting for these factors, the gap between firms expecting revenue growth and those expecting a decline remains 14 percentage points wider among AI adopters than non-adopters.
For employment expectations, the corresponding gap remains 10 percentage points wider among AI adopters.
Businesses using AI are significantly more optimistic about their future expansion.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Energy stocks are making history: The S&P 500 Energy sector took just 196 trading days to gain +50%...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Energy stocks are making history:
The S&P 500 Energy sector took just 196 trading days to gain +50% year-to-date, marking the 5th-fastest time any S&P 500 sector has reached this milestone since 1990.
For perspective, in 2022, the Energy sector surged +50% in just 94 trading days, the fastest pace recorded over the last 36 years.
By comparison, the Technology sector reached the same milestone in 133 and 160 trading days in 1996 and 1997, respectively.
Consumer Discretionary, Consumer Staples, Industrials, Materials, and Real Estate have never recorded a +50% annual gain since 1990.
The Energy sector is witnessing one of its most remarkable rallies in decades.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China's automotive industry is facing a historic slowdown: China’s automotive industry profit margi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China's automotive industry is facing a historic slowdown:
China’s automotive industry profit margin fell to 3.6% in the first 8 months of 2026, its lowest in at least 12 years.
This is now on track for its 12th consecutive annual decline.
Years of heavy investment have created severe production overcapacity, while weakening domestic demand is intensifying price wars among car manufacturers.
Meanwhile, in the first 8 months of 2026, domestic passenger vehicle sales dropped -22% YoY.
For the full year, car sales are expected to fall -22% YoY, to 18.5 million, their lowest annual total since 2014.
Now, factories have the capacity to produce a record ~62.9 million vehicles this year, more than 3 times the expected sales figure.
China’s auto industry is struggling.

item.title: @wallstengine: SPACEX MAKES HISTORY WITH FIRST STARSHIP UPPER-STAGE TOWER CATCH Ship 42 returned from orbit and wa...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
SPACEX MAKES HISTORY WITH FIRST STARSHIP UPPER-STAGE TOWER CATCH
Ship 42 returned from orbit and was caught by the launch tower arms at Starbase around 4:20 p.m. ET, roughly 22.5 hours after liftoff.
It marks the first time a spacecraft has returned from orbit and been caught by the same tower it launched from.
SpaceX had planned to catch both stages, but the Super Heavy booster was diverted offshore after its catch was aborted.
Elon Musk attributed the booster failure to slight engine underperformance and said improvements to engine performance and flight software are underway. https://x.com/SpaceX/status/2121715216597827756/video/1

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Last week's series of events which ultimately led to Jensen Huang's resignation were "set in motion" by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, per The Washington Post.
Details include:
1. Rubio initially issued a memo warning President Trump about the relationship between Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy
2. This memo was based on a CIA report which was "recasted in his own assertive terms"
3. The findings of Rubio’s memo were then leaked to the media setting off last week's chain of events
4. Jensen Huang's resignation came just 6 days after the leaks
Rubio has reportedly declined to answer reporters’ questions on his role in alerting the White House to Huang’s affair.

The AI revolution is leaving younger tech workers behind:
US software developer employment among workers aged 22-25 has fallen -20% since November 2022, when ChatGPT was launched.
Over the same period, the 26-30 age group has recorded a -4% decline.
By comparison, employment among developers aged 41-49 has surged +20%.
The 35-40 and 31-34 cohorts have grown +11% and +6%, respectively.
As a result, the employment growth gap between the youngest and the oldest group has risen to 40 percentage points.
The AI boom is destroying job opportunities for entry-level tech workers.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US existing home sales dropped -5.5% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 3.75 millio...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US existing home sales dropped -5.5% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 3.75 million, the lowest since August 2010.
Excluding the 2010 decline, this marks the lowest level since 1995.
YoY, existing home sales fell -8.8%, the largest annual decline since November 2023.
In the West, sales plunged -9.7% MoM last month, to an annualized rate of 650,000, the lowest since 1999.
Meanwhile, existing single-family home sales fell -5.8% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 3.41 million, the lowest since October 2010.
This comes as 30Y mortgage rates surged to 7.6% last month, their highest level since 2000, excluding one month in 2023.
US housing demand is collapsing.

Musk says many of the supply agreements Jensen Huang secured for Nvidia were based on personal handshakes rather than written contracts.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US inflation is diverging from the Fed’s target: US CPI Inflation has surged +30.2% since January 2...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US inflation is diverging from the Fed’s target:
US CPI Inflation has surged +30.2% since January 2020, to an all-time high.
This translates into an annualized inflation rate of +4.0% over this period.
Meanwhile, under a steady 2% annual inflation target, cumulative CPI growth would have been just +14.3%.
In other words, actual cumulative inflation is +15.9 percentage points above the target path, more than double the implied increase.
This comes as CPI has remained above 2% for 67 consecutive months.
The gap began widening again in March, as inflation has now remained above 3% for 7 consecutive months.
Asset owners are the only winners.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: On the Nvidia situation: Nvidia's board can still make things right. It has now been 48 hours since...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
On the Nvidia situation:
Nvidia's board can still make things right.
It has now been 48 hours since Jensen Huang resigned from his role as CEO, President, and board member of Nvidia.
Meanwhile, a thorough investigation has not been completed, countless critical questions are unanswered, and one of the world's greatest CEOs was forced out before the full facts of the situation were established.
In fact, the US Attorney General, the CIA, the DNI, and members of the House Intelligence Committee have also suggested that the current evidence remains inconclusive regarding whether Jensen Huang was involved in an affair with a Chinese spy.
The reality is that Jensen Huang resigned in the heat of the moment and the board acted based on speculative information.
We believe Nvidia's board, $NVDA, has a duty to shareholders to openly acknowledge that Jensen Huang could return to the company, pending a thorough investigation.
What happens in a CEO's personal life should not automatically dictate his role in a company, particularly if an investigation fails to establish national security misconduct or other wrongdoing that warrants removal.
The right move is to acknowledge that Jensen Huang is innocent until proven guilty.
Nvidia's board must do this now. It is not too late.

item.title: @wallstengine: THE FAA HAS LIFTED THE NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP The halt was lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET after more than f...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
THE FAA HAS LIFTED THE NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP
The halt was lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET after more than four hours, according to The Air Current. More than 13,000 flights were delayed or canceled, with major backlogs still affecting airports, including Chicago O’Hare and Atlanta.
CBS News reports that an update to the private communications network connecting U.S. air traffic control centers triggered a reboot, during which the FAA’s telecommunications infrastructure crashed. The network is operated by L3Harris.
The FBI is investigating whether a software update caused the failure but says there is no indication of a cyberattack or criminal activity. The cause has not been confirmed.
The disruption extended beyond the U.S., with Eurocontrol halting U.S.-bound departures from its member states and ground stops imposed at Toronto and Montreal.
Homeland Security Secretary Mullin says the government is reviewing its options, including a new air traffic control system.
This marks only the third nationwide FAA grounding, following September 11, 2001, and the January 2023 pilot notification system failure.

The disruption extended beyond the U.S., with Eurocontrol halting U.S.-bound departures from its member states and ground stops imposed at Toronto and Montreal.

BREAKING: China’s trade surplus surged +$84 billion YoY in the first 10 months of 2026, or +8.8%, to a record $1.04 trillion.
This marks the 3rd consecutive YoY increase for this period of the year, totalling +$348 billion.
China’s 2026 surplus has already surpassed every previous full-year total except 2025, when it rose to a record $1.18 trillion.
In October alone, the trade surplus increased +$17 billion YoY, to $105 billion.
This comes as exports jumped +35% YoY, to $412 billion, their 3rd-highest on record, while imports surged +42% YoY, to $307 billion, their 2nd-highest on record.
China's dominance in international trade is accelerating amid the AI investment wave.

item.title: @wallstengine: TWO MAJOR NVIDIA SHAREHOLDERS HAVE WRITTEN TO THE BOARD ASKING IT TO LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN FOR JENSEN...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TWO MAJOR NVIDIA SHAREHOLDERS HAVE WRITTEN TO THE BOARD ASKING IT TO LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN FOR JENSEN HUANG'S RETURN
Brad Gerstner, chief executive of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, have sent a joint letter to $NVDA board.
They ask the board to pursue "a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang."
"There are more questions about recent events than answers," they write, warning the board to "avoid a rush to replace Jensen that undermines and thwarts the best interests of shareholders." They say the company will be "capably led in the interim by Colette Kress and team" and that the board has time to get the decision right.
A petition site has also launched demanding the board reinstate Huang pending an independent investigation, under the line "thirty-three years deserve an answer."
Elon Musk has joined the calls for Huang's reinstatement, according to the Washington Post.
The board said earlier today it has not formally engaged any candidates and has not yet selected a search firm.
item.content:encoded:
TWO MAJOR NVIDIA SHAREHOLDERS HAVE WRITTEN TO THE BOARD ASKING IT TO LEAVE THE DOOR OPEN FOR JENSEN HUANG'S RETURN

Brad Gerstner, chief executive of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer of Atreides Management, have sent a joint letter to $NVDA board.

They ask the board to pursue "a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang."

"There are more questions about recent events than answers," they write, warning the board to "avoid a rush to replace Jensen that undermines and thwarts the best interests of shareholders." They say the company will be "capably led in the interim by Colette Kress and team" and that the board has time to get the decision right.

A petition site has also launched demanding the board reinstate Huang pending an independent investigation, under the line "thirty-three years deserve an answer."

Elon Musk has joined the calls for Huang's reinstatement, according to the Washington Post.

The board said earlier today it has not formally engaged any candidates and has not yet selected a search firm.

item.description:
THE FAA GROUND STOP HAS SPREAD ACROSS 3 CONTINENTS
Nearly 11,000 US flights have been delayed or cancelled, up from 7,000 two hours ago.
United States: every airport nationwide. Newark is running over three hours behind, Houston near three, both still increasing. Earlier, O'Hare passed three hours and Atlanta, Teterboro and JFK all exceeded two.
Canada: ground stops were imposed at Toronto and Montreal and have since cleared. Air Canada says flights to and from the United States are affected.
Europe: Eurocontrol has halted every flight departing its member states for US airports at the FAA's request.
Airlines: United says no new domestic flights will depart while the stop holds. Alaska Air has cancelled some flights and diverted others. Airline officials say some US carriers may stop operating for the rest of Friday.
Source: The Guardian, Eurocontrol, FAA, Air Canada, United, Alaska Air

THE FBI IS INVESTIGATING WHETHER A SOFTWARE UPDATE CAUSED THE FAA OUTAGE
Bloomberg reports the FBI is examining whether a software update triggered the failure that grounded every flight in the United States.
The FAA calls it a temporary telecommunications outage that led to a precautionary halt of all flights, and says every aircraft is accounted for, with international arrivals handled case by case.
Homeland Security Secretary Mullin says President Trump has been briefed, that communication has been maintained at certain levels, and that there is no cause for public alarm. Asked about the cause, he said he is "not excluding any options at this stage."
Nearly 7,000 flights have been delayed or cancelled.
Source: Bloomberg, FAA, DHS

item.title: @wallstengine: TODAY IS THE THIRD TIME THE FAA HAS GROUNDED EVERY FLIGHT IN THE COUNTRY 11 September 2001 — US air...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TODAY IS THE THIRD TIME THE FAA HAS GROUNDED EVERY FLIGHT IN THE COUNTRY
11 September 2001 — US airspace was closed for the first time in history after the terrorist attacks. All civilian traffic was halted and airborne aircraft were ordered to land at the nearest available airport.
11 January 2023 — the pilot notification system, which tells crews about hazards and runway closures, failed overnight. More than 10,000 flights were delayed. It was the first nationwide ground stop since 2001.
13 November 2026 — a communications failure hit multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centres, with the FAA also reporting impacts to radar. Nearly 7,000 flights have been delayed or cancelled so far.
Source: FAA, CNN, FlightAware
item.content:encoded:
TODAY IS THE THIRD TIME THE FAA HAS GROUNDED EVERY FLIGHT IN THE COUNTRY

11 September 2001 — US airspace was closed for the first time in history after the terrorist attacks. All civilian traffic was halted and airborne aircraft were ordered to land at the nearest available airport.

11 January 2023 — the pilot notification system, which tells crews about hazards and runway closures, failed overnight. More than 10,000 flights were delayed. It was the first nationwide ground stop since 2001.

13 November 2026 — a communications failure hit multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centres, with the FAA also reporting impacts to radar. Nearly 7,000 flights have been delayed or cancelled so far.

Source: FAA, CNN, FlightAware

item.title: @wallstengine: THE FED FLAGS AI AS A MAJOR FINANCIAL STABILITY RISK In its latest report, the Fed says elevated st...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
THE FED FLAGS AI AS A MAJOR FINANCIAL STABILITY RISK
In its latest report, the Fed says elevated stock valuations are partly driven by enthusiasm for "super intelligence" and warns that AI investment could soon surpass the 1990s telecom boom.
87% of surveyed market contacts cited AI as a financial stability risk, up from 50% in the spring, pointing to earnings disappointments, cyberattacks and complex financing.
Advanced-computing debt issuance hit $680B through October, 5x the amount in 2023, and now accounts for 31% of nonfinancial investment-grade debt issuance, up from under 6%. More than $1.1T is outstanding.
But the Fed says other obligations are growing even faster, including over $1T in future lease commitments and over $2T in take-or-pay contracts and residual value guarantees.
Hedge fund leverage is also at its highest recorded level since 2013.
The report's data cuts off on October 28, before Nvidia's latest selloff.

item.title: @wallstengine: THE FAA HAS ORDERED A NATIONAL GROUND STOP The Federal Aviation Administration has issued a nationa...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
THE FAA HAS ORDERED A NATIONAL GROUND STOP
The Federal Aviation Administration has issued a national ground stop, citing "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."
All departing traffic is to remain grounded until further notice, and inbound international flights will be managed case by case.
The FAA's own status page shows the cause spreading: ground stops at Chicago O'Hare and Midway for an equipment outage, and departure delays rising at Newark, Teterboro, Houston, Orlando, Las Vegas and Phoenix.
Seven of the eight delayed airports are flagged as FAA equipment problems, and every one is listed as increasing.
A national ground stop has happened twice in modern times, during the NOTAM system failure in January 2023 and after the September 11 attacks.
Source: FAA

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US credit stress is intensifying among the weakest-quality borrowers: Spreads on CCC-rated and lowe...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US credit stress is intensifying among the weakest-quality borrowers:
Spreads on CCC-rated and lower US corporate bonds are up to 13.3%, near the highest since the 2020 pandemic.
Since January 2026, this figure has surged +490 basis points.
As a result, these spreads have now surpassed the 2022 bear market peak of 12.9%.
For perspective, during the 2020 February-March surge, this metric peaked at 18.8%.
Meanwhile, the spread differential between CCC- and BBB-rated corporate debt has widened to ~1,200 basis points, its widest level in at least 5 years.
This means investors are demanding ~12 percentage points more in compensation to hold the lowest-rated debt rather than first-notch investment-grade corporate bonds.
Cracks are spreading quickly through the lowest-quality credit.

UBS sees a much larger opportunity for server CPUs as agentic AI scales. Q3 server CPU shipments rose 31% YoY and 6% QoQ, vs. typical seasonal growth of 3%.

Analyst Timothy Arcuri wrote: "CPU demand could be substantially higher than our current forecasts."

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US layoffs continue to slow sharply: US job cut announcements dropped -71% YoY in October, to 43,99...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US layoffs continue to slow sharply:
US job cut announcements dropped -71% YoY in October, to 43,994, the lowest October total since 2023.
Year-to-date announcements have declined -44% YoY, to 617,189, the lowest January-October total since 2022.
This is also the 8th month of 2026 with job cuts down YoY versus the corresponding month of the prior year.
Food companies led October layoffs with 9,677 cuts, while Technology has recorded the most reductions year-to-date, at 171,501, up +21% YoY.
Market and economic conditions accounted for 16,407 announced job cuts in October, or ~37% of all layoffs, bringing the year-to-date total to 130,531, overtaking AI as the most cited reason.
US employers appear to be slowing job cuts.

item.title: @wallstengine: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on why it buys compute conservatively: "Compute is the deepest business...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on why it buys compute conservatively:
"Compute is the deepest business dilemma that the company faces."
"If you buy too much ... you can financially overextend yourself. If you buy too little, then you can't support inference for customers ... you can't do the R&D."
"We actually tend to buy on the low side. We buy relatively little compute for relatively low cost ahead of time."
"If things go really well ... we have an opportunity to buy compute on the spot market. That costs more, but we're buying it in worlds where we're doing particularly well."
He compares the strategy to buying an insurance policy.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Institutional investors are extremely bullish on the US equity market: Long non-dealer positioning...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Institutional investors are extremely bullish on the US equity market:
Long non-dealer positioning in US equity futures is up to +$330 billion, its 2nd-highest on record.
This metric covers asset managers, hedge funds, Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs), and other institutional investors.
Over the last 6 months, net long positioning in US equity futures has risen by +$100 billion.
This figure is now just $10 billion below its all-time high set in 2024.
By comparison, between 2010 and 2023, institutional positioning never exceeded $150 billion.
Institutional investors are heavily exposed to US equities.

item.title: @bravosresearch: 25/ BRICS nations conduct roughly $9.6 trillion in annual trade, and the UNIT's proposed structure...
item.dc:creator: @bravosresearch
item.description:
25/ BRICS nations conduct roughly $9.6 trillion in annual trade, and the UNIT's proposed structure requires 40% gold backing.
If all that trade were settled through the UNIT, it could require around $3.8 trillion in gold value.
But, BRICS currently holds approximately 193 million ounces, implying a gold price near $20,000 an ounce to provide that backing.
So, that's roughly 5x today's price, although gold is unlikely to reach that level in a straight line.

item.title: @bravosresearch: 24/ BRICS has already introduced 10,000 sample R5 banknotes, representing the real, ruble, rupee, y...
item.dc:creator: @bravosresearch
item.description:
24/ BRICS has already introduced 10,000 sample R5 banknotes, representing the real, ruble, rupee, yuan, and rand.
For now, this is symbolic, but it offers a glimpse of what the UNIT's paper component might eventually look like.
But none of this is guaranteed because BRICS members have very different economies and no shared monetary policy framework.
However, greater use of the dollar system as a geopolitical weapon could accelerate the shift toward a multipolar alternative.
And that shift could have significant long-term implications for gold.

Over this period, $AMD rallied +44.7%, while $NVDA dropped -8.5%.
The previous record for AMD's 5-day outperformance over Nvidia since 1999 was set in April 2016, at +49.9 percentage points.
So far in 2026, $AMD is outperforming $NVDA by +184 percentage points.
This comes as AMD is up +173.3% year-to-date, while Nvidia is down -10.7%.
AMD has been a major beneficiary of Nvidia's historic volatility.

item.title: @wallstengine: FED'S GOOLSBEE: INFLATION IS BROAD-BASED & GOING THE WRONG WAY The AI data centre buildout is pushi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
FED'S GOOLSBEE: INFLATION IS BROAD-BASED & GOING THE WRONG WAY
The AI data centre buildout is pushing up prices and the Fed cannot look through inflation if demand is overheating, he told CNBC. The Fed "definitely has work to do" to maintain its credibility.
He said inflation has spread into categories where prices are not being driven by energy, and that it is proving far more persistent than expected back when it was just a matter of supply shocks.
He takes no comfort from the lack of wage inflation. Wages lag price pressures, so the labour-market read needs care, and price shocks now can show up in labour later. Services inflation and rising health care costs do not feel like they will change quickly.
Even if oil falls rapidly, he said, refining capacity remains problematic and will keep diesel and jet fuel prices elevated.
The job market is stable, maybe tightening a bit. Inflation will determine the path of rates.

TREASURY SECRETARY TELLS THE FED THIS IS AN ENERGY SUPPLY SHOCK
Scott Bessent said the Fed should understand that the current inflation is an energy supply shock, and that "to hike too much into an energy supply shock when it's coming down is a noisy number."
He said core inflation remains under control and that Iran created an energy shock the US will get to the other side of.
It comes as BofA moved this morning to forecasting hikes at each of the Fed's next 3 meetings, saying the central bank "looks further behind the curve on inflation."

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ROSENBLATT SAYS $SMCI IS CAUGHT IN NVIDIA'S "EXPORT-CONTROL CROSSFIRE"
Rosenblatt defended Super Micro after Thursday's selloff: 80% of Sept-quarter sales came from the US vs. 5.5% from Asia.
Its largest customer accounted for 44% of sales, which Rosenblatt believes is SpaceX.
Super Micro's investor relations team told Rosenblatt that the company has never supplied Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia cloud partner at the center of the chip-diversion allegations.
IR also said the company cooperated with Singaporean authorities through outside counsel. However, Singaporean authorities have described that cooperation as limited.
On the DOJ investigation, IR said the matter was previously disclosed and tied to historical OBON transactions, with no new notices received from US agencies.
An independent investigation completed in August also found no evidence that current senior management was involved in the alleged chip diversion.

item.title: @wallstengine: US intelligence officials are NOT convinced the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal was spyin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
US intelligence officials are NOT convinced the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal was spying for China, multiple sources told CNN, even though the allegation has already cost Jensen Huang his job.
Officials at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence called the spy label "not entirely accurate and over-torqued." CIA officials are not yet sure that intercepted communications show she knowingly passed information to Beijing.
Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday that no conclusions have been reached about who she is or is not, and Trump said he did not know whether it had been determined she was a spy.
Other Trump officials still regard her as a counterintelligence risk, given her access to Huang and, through him, to the president.
Note: The FBI has been investigating for at least a year and is suspicious of her switch from Chinese state TV journalist to a businesswoman with large chip-buying power. Her Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has been under a US probe since 2024 over suspected diversion of restricted chips to China.
item.content:encoded:
US intelligence officials are NOT convinced the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal was spying for China, multiple sources told CNN, even though the allegation has already cost Jensen Huang his job.

Officials at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence called the spy label "not entirely accurate and over-torqued." CIA officials are not yet sure that intercepted communications show she knowingly passed information to Beijing.

Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday that no conclusions have been reached about who she is or is not, and Trump said he did not know whether it had been determined she was a spy.

Other Trump officials still regard her as a counterintelligence risk, given her access to Huang and, through him, to the president.

Note: The FBI has been investigating for at least a year and is suspicious of her switch from Chinese state TV journalist to a businesswoman with large chip-buying power. Her Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has been under a US probe since 2024 over suspected diversion of restricted chips to China.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Retail investors bought +$730 million in Nvidia, $NVDA, stock on Tuesday, their largest d...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Retail investors bought +$730 million in Nvidia, $NVDA, stock on Tuesday, their largest daily purchase since March.
This was preceded by +$590 million on Monday and followed by +$300 million on Wednesday.
In total, retail investors bought +$1.6 billion in Nvidia shares in 3 trading days ending Wednesday, retail's largest 3-day purchase in at least 12 months.
Over the same period, the 2x leveraged long Nvidia ETF, $NVDL, attracted +$401 million in inflows, putting it on track for its largest weekly intake since November 2025.
The 2x leveraged long Nvidia ETF, $NVDU, attracted +$64 million, on track for its largest weekly inflow since February 2026.
Meanwhile, during the first 30 minutes of Thursday’s session, retail investors bought +$455 million of $NVDA stock and sold -$345 million, bringing net purchases to +$111 million, their largest in any first 30 minutes of trading on record.
Retail investors are doubling down on Nvidia.

Some officials at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence have said the characterization of Alice Huang as a Chinese spy is "not entirely accurate and over-torqued."
Officials at the CIA also are "not yet convinced" that the intelligence collection on Alice Huang so far, including intercepted communications, proves she was knowingly funneling information back to Beijing.
The FBI has reportedly been investigating this affair for at least a year.
We maintain our view that Jensen Huang and Nvidia prematurely parted ways.
A complete investigation is necessary.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US AI is generating far more revenue than Chinese AI: As of the end of September, OpenAI and Anthro...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US AI is generating far more revenue than Chinese AI:
As of the end of September, OpenAI and Anthropic had a combined estimated annualized revenue run rate of $105 billion.
This is nearly 10 times the $11 billion generated by 6 Chinese AI companies, including Alibaba, ByteDance, DeepSeek, Z Dot ai, Moonshot AI, and MiniMax.
ByteDance accounted for 36% of this figure at $4 billion.
In Q3 alone, Anthropic's sales grew +47% QoQ, to a record $17 billion.
At the same time, OpenAI revenue surged +50% to a record $10 billion.
By comparison, DeepSeek's annualized revenue run rate doubled in September, but stands at just $1 billion.
US tech firms remain in the lead of the AI race.

The S&P 500 ETF, $VOO, attracted +$16.9 billion in inflows over 5 trading days ending November 10th, the most among major US equity ETFs.
This was followed by the Nasdaq 100 ETF, $QQQ, and the total US stock market ETF, $VTI, at +$5.3 billion and +$3.3 billion, respectively.

In total, 10 major US equity ETFs attracted a massive +$37.5 billion over 5 trading days ending Tuesday.
Investors are aggressively buying the dip.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nscale has just amended its IPO filing. Here are the key new details:
It expects to spend about $21 billion to $22 billion on GPUs and compute equipment for Anthropic at its Monarch campus in West Virginia, plus $10 billion to $10.5 billion on data center and power costs for the campus's first building
Anthropic exercised its right to more compute at Monarch's second building on Sept 29
A $3.22 billion Microsoft contract was terminated after the UK power provider pulled the grid connection at its Loughton site. Its Microsoft deals totaled up to about $43.8 billion through 2033, and Nscale says the rest are unaffected
Revenue of about $307.5 million in the first nine months of 2026, up from $21.3 million a year earlier
Net loss of about $1.69 billion, up from $433.3 million
$105.8 billion of active and contracted total contract value, of which $6.4 billion is active
The AI cloud company plans to list on the NYSE as NSCL. A price range has not been set yet
It signed several multi-billion-dollar contracts with AI-native and frontier model lab customers in the second half of 2026

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investor positioning in silver is experiencing violent swings: Speculative investors sold -$2.3 bil...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investor positioning in silver is experiencing violent swings:
Speculative investors sold -$2.3 billion in silver futures over the 5 weeks ending November 3rd, according to CFTC data.
This was driven by -$2.6 billion in new short positions, partially offset by +$300 million in new longs.
Hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), alongside smaller traders such as retail investors, accounted for most of the sales, with each group reducing exposure to silver futures by ~$1.4 billion.
As a result, aggregate net long speculative positioning fell to +$8.0 billion, its lowest since January 2025.
Since its January 2026 peak, this figure has dropped by more than -$16.0 billion.
Are investors overly bearish on silver?

item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: The Nasdaq Could Be Down 20% to 40%
🔊
Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough models Risk Range™ Signals for major markets every morning. They are probable low and high levels based on price, volume and volatility, and he uses it to decide when to buy and when to sell.
For the S&P 500, the range is 7313 to 7688, he said on The Macro Show.
Even a rally to the top of that range would leave the S&P below its prior peak, which Keith calls a big lower high. Lower highs are how a Bearish TREND plays out.
The Nasdaq is still in an 8% drawdown, including yesterday’s bounce. Keith said it could be down 20% to 40% by the end of it.
He plans to buy gold but is waiting for the signal that it’s done going down.
“I just don’t know when,” he said. “I have the humility to say that. I don’t have price targets.”
Keith said he doesn’t have a 2027 outlook either, and whether he buys gold on Dec. 27 or Jan. 13 doesn’t matter to him.
“That’s not how you play the game,” he said.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Think of hedging like insurance on your house. The worst day to buy it is during somebody else's hu...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Think of hedging like insurance on your house.
The worst day to buy it is during somebody else's hurricane. Everyone wants it, so you pay up.
The best day is when nobody thinks a hurricane is possible. Implied volatility flips from a premium to a discount and protection gets cheap.
That's when you add. Incrementally.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US small businesses are signaling more inflation ahead: The proportion of US small firms planning t...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US small businesses are signaling more inflation ahead:
The proportion of US small firms planning to raise prices over the next 3 months rose +6 percentage points in October, to 37%, the most since July 2022.
Excluding the post-pandemic surge in 2021 and 2022, this marks the highest reading since 2008.
By comparison, this figure did not exceed 30% between 2009 and 2019.
Furthermore, 33% of small firms raised prices over the last 3 months, the 3rd-highest reading since March 2023.
Meanwhile, 17% of business owners pointed to inflation as their single most important problem, up from 12% a year ago.
Small businesses are preparing for further price hikes as inflationary pressures mount.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US inflationary pressures are broadening: Core CPI inflation surged to a 3-month annualized rate of...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US inflationary pressures are broadening:
Core CPI inflation surged to a 3-month annualized rate of +3.75% in October, its highest reading since April 2024.
This marks its 3rd consecutive monthly increase, up from +1.64% in July.
At the same time, core services less shelter inflation, also known as Supercore CPI and closely monitored by the Fed, rose to a 3-month annualized rate of +5.45%, its highest since mid-2024.
The weighted proportion of CPI components rising at an annualized rate above 2% soared to 76% last month, the largest percentage since August 2022.
This figure has risen +17 percentage points since July, marking its sharpest 3-month increase since early 2021.
The Fed's fight against inflation is far from over.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Our message to Nvidia's board: Do not fire Jensen Huang. There is no clear replacement for Jensen H...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Our message to Nvidia's board:
Do not fire Jensen Huang.
There is no clear replacement for Jensen Huang. We are confident that his departure would ultimately be a net negative for Nvidia, its shareholders, and the AI Revolution.
First, take a look at the data. History also suggests that removing a successful CEO will come with a significant cost.
A study of 187 forced CEO departures from S&P 1500 companies found that removing outperforming CEOs resulted in negative long-term stock returns. This case would be no different, in our view.
Jensen Huang is the definition of an outperforming CEO. Nvidia's board must not make a decision in the heat of the moment.
The board should take the time to conduct a thorough investigation and consult with shareholders, with a strong emphasis on the latter.
Quite literally, Nvidia's board should convene a special shareholder meeting and hold an advisory vote on this decision. This is the most consequential CEO controversy in world history. Shareholders deserve a say.
In addition, Nvidia's stock, $NVDA, is now down -35% in 26 trading days, nearly half of which is a result of the recent scandal.
We believe Jensen Huang's potential removal as CEO is now ~80% priced in.
Why take an action with massive downside potential when the market has already priced in much of that risk?
The downside of retaining Huang may be limited, while the potential upside is tremendous.
Lastly, history shows that retaining Jensen Huang could still lead to a favorable outcome. In 2019, Amazon retained Jeff Bezos as CEO after his extramarital affair became public, and the company's stock subsequently surged +108% by 2021.
Personal misconduct should not be ignored, but it must also be distinguished from corporate wrongdoing and weighed against the consequences of removing an executive who is instrumental to the company's success.
We believe Jensen Huang is an irreplaceable part of Nvidia and the AI Revolution more broadly.
Once the dust settles, firing Jensen Huang would prove to be a costly mistake.
It is time to pause and consult your shareholders.

item.title: @Hedgeye_HGRO: I say welcome to the party, pal! In all seriousness. $AMD has been well positioned for awhile now a...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye_HGRO
item.description:
I say welcome to the party, pal!
In all seriousness. $AMD has been well positioned for awhile now as a structural winner in AI as most of the compute workloads are moving from training to inferencing. For example, the more agents that get created and used, that workload is mostly on CPUs (with $AMD and $INTC among the leaders, though the latter is flailing with execution issues)
Supply constraints have moved within the AI supply chain from GPUs to CPUs, foundry and substrates. So CPUs are in short supply and in high demand
$AMD also had a stellar 3rd quarter earnings report last week that was completely drowned out by the tsunami of liquidation we saw in tech.
That’s why I bought it on Monday

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US pension funds are heavily concentrated in technology stocks: The technology sector accounts for...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US pension funds are heavily concentrated in technology stocks:
The technology sector accounts for 44% of total US pension fund equity allocation, according to a Bloomberg analysis of more than 70 pension funds.
This percentage has more than doubled since 2015.
Pension fund equity allocation to technology is now larger than that of the next 3 sectors combined.
By comparison, Financials represent 16%, followed by Healthcare at 12%, Industrials at 11%, and Consumer stocks at 10%.
To put this into perspective, the Consumer sector was these funds' largest allocation in 2014, at ~20%.
US pension funds are more exposed to technology stocks than ever.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Cost effectiveness of AI is becoming a hot topic. As AI adoption accelerates, the focus is increasi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Cost effectiveness of AI is becoming a hot topic.
As AI adoption accelerates, the focus is increasingly shifting from simply building more powerful models to maximizing the value generated by every dollar spent.
Not every task requires the most expensive or advanced AI model.
In fact, the global AI inference software market is projected to grow from $21.1 billion in 2026 to $80.9 billion by 2033, representing +283% growth.
As companies deploy AI at scale, reducing costs without sacrificing performance will be increasingly important.
The next phase of AI is about efficiency, not just computing power.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The perceived probability among US consumers that the unemployment rate will be higher in...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The perceived probability among US consumers that the unemployment rate will be higher in 1 year increased +1.5 percentage points in October, to 45.3%, the highest since April 2020.
This also marks the 3rd-highest reading on record, surpassed only by the initial pandemic surge in March and April 2020.
Since January 2025, this metric has risen +11.3 percentage points.
Among age groups, consumers under 40 are the most pessimistic, with the perceived probability of higher unemployment at 48.9%, the 2nd-highest reading on record.
By income, this figure among those earning over $100,000 rose to 51.5%, the 2nd-highest reading on record, surpassed only by the 53.9% recorded in March 2020.
Americans are worried about their jobs.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The Machine Learning market is seeing accelerating growth. The global machine learning market is no...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The Machine Learning market is seeing accelerating growth.
The global machine learning market is now projected to grow from ~$100 billion in 2025 to ~$684 billion by 2033.
This implies a CAGR of +27.2% from 2025 to 2033.
As AI evolves, the focus is shifting toward AI models that can continuously learn, retain knowledge, and adapt to new tasks.
This represents a fundamental shift from AI systems that rely primarily on knowledge acquired during training to systems capable of improving through experience.
As adoption accelerates, demand for machine learning software, hardware, and services is expected to increase substantially.
We are watching this market.

item.title: @wallstengine: $GOOGL TESTS NEW GEMINI 4 FLASH MODEL CODENAMED "HYDROGEN" INTERNALLY - BI Google is letting employ...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL TESTS NEW GEMINI 4 FLASH MODEL CODENAMED "HYDROGEN" INTERNALLY - BI
Google is letting employees test a new Gemini AI model called Hydrogen, which a Google engineer described as
"very capable, fast and efficient."
The model is available to staff through Google's internal development platform, Jetski, which has previously been used to test models ahead of public releases.
Hydrogen appears to be the next Gemini 4 Flash model, focused on delivering faster responses and lower costs than Google's more powerful models, such as Argon and the newly released Carbon.
Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon on Tuesday, positioning it as its most capable model yet, particularly for cybersecurity and complex tasks involving multiple steps.
Both Argon and Carbon are currently limited to paying users, while Google's previous Flash models have been available for free in the Gemini app.
It's not yet clear when Hydrogen will launch publicly or whether it will be offered for free.
Source: Business Insider

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Berkshire Hathaway is making a historic comeback: Berkshire Hathaway outperformed the S&P 500 by +1...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Berkshire Hathaway is making a historic comeback:
Berkshire Hathaway outperformed the S&P 500 by +19.2 percentage points over the 1 month ending Thursday, its largest rolling monthly outperformance since 2010.
This also ranks as the 4th-largest such outperformance in 30 years.
By comparison, its biggest monthly rolling outperformance occurred during the 2008 Financial Crisis, at +29.6 percentage points.
As of Tuesday's close, the performance gap narrowed to +16.9 percentage points, but it still ranked as one of the largest since 1996.
This comes as Berkshire Hathaway's Class B stock has surged +13.2% over the last month, to an all-time high, while the S&P 500 has declined -3.7% over the same period.
To put this into perspective, Berkshire was underperforming the S&P 500 by -14.3 percentage points in May 2026.
Berkshire Hathaway appears strong, even without Warren Buffett as CEO.

item.title: @wallstengine: Anthropic is projected to generate ~$19.3B in Q4 revenue, according to an analyst note circulating...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Anthropic is projected to generate ~$19.3B in Q4 revenue, according to an analyst note circulating online.
That's up ~14% from Q3 and roughly 9.5x from a year ago. Still, it implies a ~$77B annualized pace, below its $81B October run rate.
Anthropic's IPO filing said usage typically slows during the winter holidays.
Its latest model, Opus 5.5, also reduced the cost per task by ~40%, while price cuts already reduced Q3 revenue by ~$600M.

item.title: @DougKass: Chip: In this tweet I will briefly explain why my hedge fund @seabreezelp has only one outside rese...
item.dc:creator: @DougKass
item.description:
Chip:
In this tweet I will briefly explain why my hedge fund @seabreezelp has only one outside research subscription - and that is to @hedgeye lengthy suite of products.
I will also defend and explain my strong support of @KeithMcCullough and his (hockey) tough, hard hitting approach to marketing and delivering Hedgeye's recommendations and points of view.
I graduated with an MBA from Wharton where I learned how to model companies and be a fundamental security analyst. I became Kidder Peabody's housing analyst where I perfected my analytical craft. From there I moved to Putnam where I followed financials and ultimately was an Economist.
In the above capacities I differentiated (I was always far from the herd) myself by avoiding "group stink" and offering a contrarian view (my first research report at Kidder was a sell recommendation on a very hot mobile home industry sector). My negative industry analysis on Fleetwood, Skyline and Champion homes was 65 pages long. (Later on in my career I appeared in Alan Abelson's Barrons column more than 50 times, delivering contrarian and often bearish analysis. I wrote five editorials for Barrons and was featured on the cover as well as writing editorials in The Financial Times- almost always of a non consensus bent.
The common denominator at the two jobs (Kidder and Putnam) was hard hitting and differentiated research.
At Putnam in the 1970s, it was an era of "stock pickers" led by Fidelity Magellan's Peter Lynch and my boss Putnam's Jerry "The Chief" Jordan.
Over time (and decades later), active management lost favor and passive investment management took over. Peter Lynch and Jerry Jordan's funds were replaced by Index funds (ETFs, Quant Funds and Pods) that worshipped not on fundamental analysis but at the altar of price momentum.
Company spread sheets (modelling) were partiallly replaced by algorithms and machines - who know everything about price but nothing about value.
I recognized the metamorphosis of the investment business and needed and sought a way to introduce quantitative measurements to complement my fundamental security analysis.
I discovered fractals and, in time, the best practitioner for integrating fractals and quantitative analysis into my fundamental Stock Market equation - @KeithMcCullough at @hedgeye.
Earlier I referenced Hedgeye's suite of products. I also actively utilize their fundamental research product which is differentiated and often contrary. ($MTP, an investment short at our fund, was brought to my attention by Hedgey's research, there have been many others). They don't follow the institutional script.
As to Keith's delivery - it reflects what he is up against, an institutional community of research which is non differentiated and conflicted... and panelists and guests on business media that are generally perma bullish, non rigorous, inconsistent in process, don't time stamp, takes no ownership of oft repeated losers and (invariably) leads retail investors to large drawdowns in every single cycle "when the tide goes out" (in part because they have no risk management discipline). They are generally "talking heads" who polish their images (for free) in @CNBC and elsewhere - regardless of contribution or degree of value.
Let me make it clear Chip - going up against the establishment is a difficult endeavour. Succeeding in the manner in which @hedgeye had done is next to impossible. Whereas @DivesTech @fundstrat and sell side research firms like Goldman Sachs and Bankamerica "pay for play" and are invited daily on FIN TV, a contrarian shop is not. They don't have access as they piss off the establishment. And in the case of @hedgeye they dont want to go on Fin TV.
Let me give you a metaphor. My sister Deb Kass is an extraordinary famous artist. She started out competing in an all male art world in the late 1970s. She and other female artists had virtually no or limited access to gallery shows which mainly exhibited male body of work. As such she faced near insurmountable hurdles. But she persevered and produced brave, outspoken and unique product and has become a legendary figure in the art world - her next retrospective will be at The Barnes Museum in Philly next year. (She taught at Yale for many years, Keith graduated Yale - something also in common).
And like @KeithMcCullough she fought hard, is tough and was her best salesperson.
Oy yo, baby! (I am referencing her famous Oy Yo sculpture which resides on the front lawn of the Brooklyn Museum of Art, in the front of the Jewish Museum in Philadelphia and at the Iris Cantor Cultural Center at Stanford University. @DeborahKaty
Chip, you tweeted that in supporting Keith I am complicit. I have no clue what you even mean.
Nonetheless, I hope you now understand my subscription and defense of @hedgeye @RPKInvestor @HedgeyeDJ - and why I totally disagree with your characterization of Hedgeye and myself.
The difference between you and me - on this subject -is that you deliver fifteen words of view whereas I expand my explanation so you and other people fully understand my position.

They are generally "talking heads" who polish their images (for free) in @CNBC and elsewhere - regardless of contribution or degree of value.

Let me make it clear Chip - going up against the establishment is a difficult endeavour. Succeeding in the manner in which @hedgeye had done is next to impossible. Whereas @DivesTech @fundstrat and sell side research firms like Goldman Sachs and Bankamerica "pay for play" and are invited daily on FIN TV, a contrarian shop is not. They don't have access as they piss off the establishment. And in the case of @hedgeye they dont want to go on Fin TV.

Let me give you a metaphor. My sister Deb Kass is an extraordinary famous artist. She started out competing in an all male art world in the late 1970s. She and other female artists had virtually no or limited access to gallery shows which mainly exhibited male body of work. As such she faced near insurmountable hurdles. But she persevered and produced brave, outspoken and unique product and has become a legendary figure in the art world - her next retrospective will be at The Barnes Museum in Philly next year. (She taught at Yale for many years, Keith graduated Yale - something also in common).

And like @KeithMcCullough she fought hard, is tough and was her best salesperson.

Oy yo, baby! (I am referencing her famous Oy Yo sculpture which resides on the front lawn of the Brooklyn Museum of Art, in the front of the Jewish Museum in Philadelphia and at the Iris Cantor Cultural Center at Stanford University. @DeborahKaty

Chip, you tweeted that in supporting Keith I am complicit. I have no clue what you even mean.

Nonetheless, I hope you now understand my subscription and defense of @hedgeye @RPKInvestor @HedgeyeDJ - and why I totally disagree with your characterization of Hedgeye and myself.

The difference between you and me - on this subject -is that you deliver fifteen words of view whereas I expand my explanation so you and other people fully understand my position.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global central banks bought +321 tonnes of gold in Q3 2026, their largest quarterly purch...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global central banks bought +321 tonnes of gold in Q3 2026, their largest quarterly purchase since Q4 2024.
This also marks their 5th-largest quarterly purchase on record.
Central bank gold purchases were up +8% from +296 tonnes acquired in Q2 2026 and up +453% from Q1 2026.
By comparison, the 5-year quarterly average stands at +227 tonnes.
China and Poland led Q3 demand, adding +63 tonnes and +40 tonnes, respectively.
Year-to-date, global central banks have purchased +675 tonnes of gold, up +6% from the same period in 2025.
Central banks are aggressively buying the dip in gold.

item.title: @wallstengine: $IBM announced Nighthawk r3, designed to execute 10,000 quantum operations across 520 programmable...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$IBM announced Nighthawk r3, designed to execute 10,000 quantum operations across 520 programmable qubits.
It plans to connect two r3 chips into a 1,040-qubit system in 2027.
Current r2 has executed 34B circuits, with speedups of up to 19x over previous IBM processors.
